			"Don't listen to him." she chuckled, ruffling his fur. "You can stay here and snuggle with granny Eileen, alright?"
			"Okay! Her house, her rules." Sparky grinned. Connor chuckled, and relented.
			"So... tell me if I'm being presumptuous, but I'm guessing, with a name like Eileen and a Catholic service, your family were Irish?"
			"Oh, you bet." she smiled. "My parents were from Limerick. Moved to London in the late 1920s. My dad was a Protestant, but he never gave a shit about religion, so my mum brought me up Catholic."
			Connor nodded. "I grew up in Derry. Bogside."
			She looked at him sadly. "I'm guessing, based on how old you are..."
			"Yeah." he sighed. "It's fine. I survived, anyway."
			He cleared his throat. "So... your parents moved here in the 20s, so that makes you... what, 40?"
			"Charmer." she grinned. "I'm 82 years young."
			"Any stories? I bet you have a few."
			She paused, before raising her fists and showing the knuckles. Old, white scars covered them.
			"Were you a fighter?" he asked.
			"Boxer. Women's boxing. I was pretty good, too." she chuckled.
			"I learned kickboxing from my uncle." Connor nodded. "Still keep it up when I can."
			"Well, if I could stand for more than two seconds, I'd whoop your arse." she grinned. "But the boxing was only half the story."
			She pulled out a photo album, and showed a photo.
			She was a very confident young woman, clearly. She was wearing a tank top that showed off her muscles, with a neat bob the only sign of femininity. Her fists were presented - and her knuckles were tattooed.
			'LOVE' read her left. 'HATE' read her right.
			"Damn." Connor nodded.
			"I know, I was gorgeous." she laughed. "Anyway, the tattoos were stupid. So, one night, I got drunk as a skunk, and grabbed a potato peeler--"
			"Ew!" Connor cringed, laughing. "Jesus, Eileen."
			She cackled, before coughing again. She flipped the page to show another photo.
			This one was more artistic. She was perched atop a classic motorbike, wearing a leather jacket that fluttered in the wind. Her hair was a little bit longer - and she was smiling cheekily.
			"My old fella took that one." she nodded. "Reggie."
			"Was he... was he Steve's dad?" Connor asked.
			"Nah. Truth be told... I don't know who his dad was." she shook her head. "After Reggie passed, I had a wild few weeks. 9 months later, little Steve came along."
			He nodded softly. "Grief can be hard."
			At that, a honking snore shook both. Sparky shuffled slightly, resting his head on Eileen.
			"Lazy little mite." she beamed.
			"He's had some exciting evenings."
			She smiled. "Anyway... see the fag in my hand?"
			Connor nodded, as she began to chuckle.
			"Well... I was in this biker club, right? I was the only girl. We'd do this thing where we'd let our fags burn as far down to the skin as we could; I'd always let it burn out in my knuckles before I'd even think of losing. I was more man than any of 'em."
			Connor laughed. "So, to be clear, I'm currently eating Chinese with the biggest badass in all of Drackhill?"
			"That's your claim to fame, love." she smirked.
			Connor leaned in a little, taking a closer look.
			"Oi - my eyes are up there." she snarked, pointing.
			"Don't flatter yourself." he grinned. "I was looking at the bike."
			"Cheeky sod!" she laughed, slapping his arm. "You're a bit of a grease monkey, I take it?"
			"Well, my day job is a mechanic. A classic like that - reminds me of my old cruiser." he shrugged, before taking out his phone.
			First, he showed her his original bike - the one he rode on the night he died. The night they killed him, and---no, Connor. Don't think about it. Don't let it hurt. Not now.
			"That's a sweet bike." she nodded. "I love those afterburners. Bet you get loads of girls begging for a ride - *on the bike,* before you get your mind in the gutter."
			Connor cackled. "I don't ride her anymore - lost her in a--in an accident."
			"Oh, dear." she sighed. "A ride like that... what a shame. She's a Valiant, isn't she?"
			"Valiant Thunderbird." Connor nodded. "Yours was a Renegade, I'm guessing?"
			"You really know your bikes." she smiled, impressed.
			"I've got this one now, anyway." he swiped, showing his newer, black and red sports bike.
			"Ooh! Now she's a pretty girl." Eileen grinned. "Sleek as you like, she is. Is that a Japanese?"
			"Yeah, she's from the Zaibatsu Motor Company." Connor nodded. "She's a Vanta S4."
			"Nice. Never rode a Zaibatsu, to be fair - but I heard they're smooth sailors."
			"I like her. My Thunderbird was pretty good - she had a bigger kick when you got her going. But the Vanta turns like a snake, and if you're smart with the afterburner, you can outpace the Thunderbird. Plus, her fuel economy is something else. If she were out of the box, I'd take a Valiant, no question - but if you give her some customisation, she'll give you a lot back."
			"Heh... I bet she wouldn't hold a candle to my Renegade." Eileen chuckled. "The Thunderbird was always overblown, in my opinion. It was the poor man's Renegade, no offence."
			"None taken. I've always dreamed of riding a Renegade, to be honest."
			A cheeky grin flashed over her face. "You know... she's still in my garage."
			"No way." Connor gasped. "You could make a sweet buck selling a vintage Renegade."
			"I could never part with her." Eileen shrugged. "Hey... wanna see her up close?"
			"Does the pope shit in the woods?"
			She burst out laughing, and then choked a little. She cleared her throat, and laughed some more.
			"God, you're gonna be the death of me, kid."
			Connor looked away awkwardly.
			"I'm joking! Jesus." she grinned, before wheeling herself forwards. Sparky made a big stretch, as he came down from the sofa and trotted by her side.
			"Ooh, biiiig stretch!" she cooed.
			"Hm? Yeah, it was pretty big." the wolf shrugged.

			"There she is." Eileen gestured, waving her hand at the genuine article before them.
			"Oh. My. God." Connor gasped, rushing over.
			It put the Thunderbird to shame. If you told Connor that the Renegade was a supernatural entity that refused to look as good on camera as it did in person, he'd believe you before his twin hearts could finish a beat.
			It was gorgeous. Thick, yet soft leather on the seats that could take years of wear before tearing. Her exhaust pipe snaked from the engine, with her chrome torso shining against her dark red decals. Her headlight looked like the eye of a Cyclops, and her handlebars were wide like wings.
			"Go on, hop aboard. She's itching for an arse on her seat." Eileen chuckled.
			Connor didn't hesitate. He leapt over her, and sank into the leather. His feet found the footrests without delay, and he leaned forward to grip the handles.
			"Now *this* is a bike." Connor grinned. "Do you take her out much?"
			"How thick are you, exactly?" she tilted her head, pointing down at her wheelchair.
			"Oh, shit, sorry--"
			She burst out laughing, wheeling up to his side.
			"I last rode her in '94. She hasn't been out since '09." she explained. "Steve took her out for a spin every now and then, but she's been sat here gathering dust for too long now."
			"If only you knew a mechanic who specialised in bikes, who could tune her up free of charge." Connor grinned. "Seriously, if you'd be up for it, I'd love to work on her. Fixing up a Renegade is a dream come true for me."
			"Heh... you know what, I might take you up on that." she chuckled.
			They returned to the lounge, and went back into the picture book.
			She flipped the page, and regaled him with another tale - this one, of how she was arrested for drunken disorder, and needed several cops to bring her down.
			Connor smiled and listened, despite the pit in his stomach.
			It was wrong. It was right.
			For the first time in a while, he was grateful to go on patrol that night.

		Supper with Eileen

		SCENE
			"Jesus fuckin' Christ."

			"Evening, sir." Nina nodded as she approached. "How bad is it?"
			"Bad. Very, very bad." he shuddered, ushering her in.
			"Holy..." she gasped at the sight.

			"Is there anything on a serial killer called 'Pig Head?' And for the record, that's the last time I'm gonna use that stupid name. Even 'Grom' is a better codename."
			"Yes... he's well known in the intelligence world. His real name is Christopher Percival Bacon."
			"...wait. Chris P. Bacon? Are you fucking with me?!"
			"Of course I'm fucking with you!" Ivan laughed jovially. "No, they have no name or alias on this guy. But apparently, he targets pig farmers. According to surviving witnesses, he wears some kind of pig mask... well, they say he has a pig's head, but the NCA think it's a mask."
			"The NCA probably think I'm just a guy who eats spinach." Connor quipped. "Alright... let's see if we can track down the Notorious P-I-G."
			"Says here the guy's deranged." Ivan noted. "Watch yourself."

		Larder
		______________________________
		SCENE
			The pair came to a stop outside a log cabin in the middle of nowhere. Their eyes burned, as they scanned the site.
			"The pigs are all milling about in a den underground." Sparky noted. "Pigs and humans are surprisingly similar - I'm struggling to figure out who Pig Head might be."
			"Amy Swinehouse'll be in there *somewhere.*" Connor shrugged.
			"You're gonna keep calling him funny names, aren't you?"
			"Of course I am." Connor chuckled. "OI! Luke Skyporker! You in?!"
			He saw a humanoid heartbeat quicken, before it raced towards a cabinet.
			"Alright... go time." Connor grinned.
			A kick ripped out from him, smashing down the door. The twin Werewolves stormed in, and rushed downstairs.
			There, Connor's own hearts fluttered in horror.
			Not from the fact that this 'cellar' was a lot bigger than he'd expected - it was more like a man-made cave.
			Not from the several corpses dangling from even more meathooks - well, not *just* them. Those were pretty spooky too.
			Not from the several squealing, very clearly angry pigs.
			Not from the butcher's table with several *more* corpses, who had been filleted.
			Not even from the altar with several candles - and the skull of a pig held in place, in reverence; in a way that uncomfortably reminded him of Sunday Mass.
			No, the freakiest part... was the hulking lump of a man, grotesque and rotund - with a pig's head.
			"Okay... the name actually makes a bit more sense now." he shuddered. "So... I guess a joke about 'long pork' would be in bad taste, eh?"
			Pig Head snorted angrily through his snout, chewing and swallowing a chunk of raw human meat.
			"Haha! Taste... I didn't even plan that one, it just... *ahem.* I make jokes when I'm nervous."
			"You... we heard stories about you..." Pig Head growled. The way his mouth moved as he spoke - in a surprisingly articulate way - only further unnerved the Werewolves.
			"'We?'" Connor pressed.
			"The Pigs speak of you."
			Connor cleared his throat again, looking down at the herd of swine. A particularly grumpy-looking sow was staring at him intently.
			"Um... they spoke of me?"
			"Can they talk, too?" Sparky tilted his head. "Hi! Um... my name is 'Not the Big Bad Wolf.' That's right! You can build as many straw houses as you like."
			"That was good. That was really good." Connor grinned. "We should quip more often."
			"You kill the stink." Pig Head nodded.
			"The... stink?"
			"Yes... you've killed so many of them. We are impressed."
			"You're talking about Super-Agents?"
			The Pig tilted his Head. "Super-what?"
			"Wait... you mean humans, don't you?"
			"Yes..." he--or it, maybe--grinned savagely. "But why? The Pigs don't know, not yet. Is it friend or foe?"
			"Listen... you've killed people. But you're also... clearly ill. So, I'll give you this one offer. Surrender, now."
			A wet, honking snort noise filled the cave. "Foe? Foe! FOE! The Pigs scream! PIGS SCREAM! Hungry. HUNGRY. HUNGRYYYY!"
			"I'll take that as a 'no.'" Connor chuckled darkly. "Okay, then, Hamuel L. Jackson - let's dance, motherfucker."
			The pigs around them became agitated - very agitated. Then, they pounced.

			The first hog to jump in was young, and had a spring in his trotters. He moved with surprising agility, clamping his tusks on Connor's forearm.
			The suspicious sow chose to take on Sparky - bull-rushing into his hide and trying her best to gore him.
			Connor sent a kick to his pig's underbelly, sending it flying back and crashing down. He heard a cacophony of cries - tucked away in the corner were a gaggle of piglets - younger siblings to their hotheaded brother.
			"Spartacus!" he barked. "Careful not to kill, okay?"
			"Oh, but when we buy bacon from the shop, that's fine." he snarked. "Alright."
			He turned on his side, and swept the sow's legs out from under her.
			"KRRRRUUUUUURRR!" Pig Head roared, charging in. He turned, and drove something down.
			It didn't hurt. Not really, not at first. The second swing was similar.
			Then both hit his nervous system, and he howled in pain.
			Pig Head pulled his arms back, wrenching his twin cleavers from Connor's clavicles.
			He knelt down, and crossed his arms, morphing a bandage over the tears to stop the bleeding. Then, his eyes blazed.
			"Alright, Piggy Stardust. You want a fight? I'll give you a fight."
			Pig Head responded with a guttural snort that might have been laughter. He raised both cleavers, the blades glinting in the dim candlelight.
			Connor shifted mass from his blood to his fists, thickening them into calcified gauntlets. He pounced forward like a cannonball, and drove a devastating uppercut to the swine-faced maniac.
			"STOP FIGHTING ME!" he squealed. "YOU'RE ON MY SIDE! KILLING THE HUMANS!"
			"I kill *monsters,* porky." Connor snapped back. "You kill innocent people. That's not remotely the same."
			"Not innocent! They're all bad! ALL BAD!" Pig Head cried. "They hurt the Pigs! Made ME hurt the Pigs! BAD, BAD PIG HEAD!"
			He bashed himself in the face with a rock, as Connor grimaced.
			"TWENTY YEARS! TWENTY YEARS I LISTENED TO THEM SCREAM! AND NO ONE CARED! NO ONE!"
			The cleavers glinted in the candlelight, as he swung them towards the Werewolf.
			Connor snarled as they cut into his hide, slicing his abdomen. He raised his gauntlets and brought them down, and heard a satisfying *CRACK!* as Pig Head's right elbow buckled.
			"GAAAGGH! KRRRRUUUUUUUURRR!" the monster screamed. He brought down the other cleaver, and it narrowly missed Connor's head.
			Connor cartwheeled, scaling upwards. He gripped the boar-face's head with his hands, and drove his consciousness forward.
			An erratic man like that - Connor hoped to find a weakness. Or at least, a method to the madness. Some means to predict his attacks.
			Instead, all he heard was a chorus of oinking. He fell back, clutching his ears.
			"KILL THE STINK! KILL THE STINK! DO IT NOW, YOU BASTARD! AVENGE ME!" the pig skull at the altar roared.
			Connor shook his head, banishing the voice. Perhaps, mind-merging with a psychotic killer wasn't the *best* idea, in hindsight.
			"Who were you?" he asked, catching his breath. "And what happened to you?"
			Pig Head sobbed, crawling towards the altar.
			"I'm sorry. I'm sorry. I'm sorry." it whispered to the skull.
			"Hey, Connor?" Sparky barked, having just bodyslammed another boar. "Can we wrap this up?"
			"Who were you?" Connor pressed.
			"Evil. Bad. BAD!" the porcine hulk blubbered. "I hurt the pigs! And they knew! Every night, they screamed into my ears! I couldn't take it!"
			"So... you were what, an abattoir?"
			"Murderer. Call it what it was. Murder."
			"You've murdered a lot of people recently, Hamlet." Connor scowled.
			"AND THEY DESRVED IT! ALL OF THEM!"
			Connor readied his fists for another bout. "Alright, former abattoir turned psycho cannibal, I get that bit. I even get the whole 'haunted by dead pigs, goes after pig farmers' shtick. But... and I mean this respectfully... what the fuck is up with your face?"
			"Kind man..." the swineface smiled. "Taught me how to listen to the Pigs. Then he stuck his knives in my face and made me... better."
			Pig Head reached for his snout, and honked it like a clown's nose. He let out an oink, and giggled.
			Connor's eyes flicked to the pig skull on the altar. Then back to the man in front of him.
			"Totenshweine over there. Was it---"

			"One more chance. Come quietly, and maybe we can get you the help you *actually* need."
			"NOOO! NO! SHUT UP!" Pig Head screamed, lunging forward. "SHUT UP SHUT UP SHUT UP!"

			"Alright..." Connor snarled. "No more 'last chances.'"
			His wristblades reformed into the chitinous gauntlets, and he parried a cleaver-swing with a heavy strike.
			The air shook from the impact force. His bludgeon cracked and weakened - while the cleaver's blade snapped, and Pig Head's arm flew backwards.
			He pressed his advantage - stomping his foot on the monster's knee, feeling it pop from the force.
			A leap up, delivering the mother of all headbutts to Pig Head's chin. 
			Then, push-stepping off of the shoulders, he brought the fists down on his enemy's snout.
			Cartilage crunched. Pig Head howled - not in anger this time, but in pain. Real, human pain.
			Connor somersaulted over his rotund quarry, landing on the altar. He held the skull aloft.
			"Hey, Oink Floyd! Surrender now, or Daddy Pig gets it!"
			"PLEASE!" he screamed, his voice cracking and weak with blood-filled sinuses. "PLEASE! I'M SORRY! I'M--"
			Connor hesitated. The Rage was there, pounding in his skull, demanding he finish it. But the man was broken. Beaten. Bleeding.
			He threw the skull forwards. Pig Head leapt forward, catching it. He looked up, and...
			Connor's boot crashed into his temple. His eyes rolled back, before another strike - this one to the back of the neck, right were spine meets skull. Then, Connor jumped in the air in a backflip - and drove his knees into the back of the lungs. Finally, he grabbed the tuft of hair at the scalp, yanked the killer's head in the air, and slammed it back down into the corner of the altar. The stone cracked, as Pig Head finally went limp.
			"Spartacus!" Connor called out. "How are the pigs?"

			"Well, I guess if Napoleon Boarnaparte isn't issuing orders, then--"
			"Okay, stop. He's unconscious, he can't appreciate the puns anymore." Sparky sighed.
			"Alright, alright - you know, trying to stop me will only make it worse? It's the Boarbra Streisand eff---"

			"OW! Okay, fair." Connor chuckled, plucking a bolt from his arm. "I didn't even know you could do the crossbow trick."
			Sparky grinned, as the back-mounted ballista dissolved and re-absorbed into his hide.

			Before another minute of victory could pass, the moment was killed.
			"ARMED POLICE! SHOW ME YOUR HANDS!" Naismith roared.
			"Oh, look! More pigs!" Connor quipped. His and Sparky's armours thickened, as they bull-rushed forwards, knocking the officers down.
			Naismith stumbled to his feet, frantically giving chase--no. They were already long gone.
			"Jesus Christ..." he spat, before heading back downstairs.
			"This... is a lot to process." Nina shuddered.
			"Hey, leave it to the NCA. They wanna deal with the paperwork here? Let 'em." he chuckled darkly.

			"Why didn't you kill him?" Sparky asked, as the two arrived in the city's outskirts.
			Connor paused for a moment. "Because people like that... they're not responsible for what they're doing, not really. Okay, he hurt a lot of people - but from his perspective, he was saving sentient beings that were being tortured and murdered. And he was ill."
			"We need to find out who changed his face." Sparky nodded. "That's the real criminal here."
			"Agreed." Connor nodded. "Now... we'd better go on patrol."
			"Ugh..." Sparky groaned.
			"Fair's fair."
			"You got all the cool fighting! I had to play sheepdog with a bunch of things that very much weren't sheep!"
			"How do you think I feel? It's gonna be a good week or so before I can stomach a bacon sarnie again."

			At the back of Connor's mind though, a gnawing feeling persisted.
			Why wasn't he horrified? Why wasn't he in shock?

			Why was this normal, now?

		Porky Pies

		SCENE

			"NO! No, please don't!" Mary screamed, as Danny froze in terror.
			"Her next. One."
			"Please! Please don't do this."
			"Two."
			"ALRIGHT! I'll talk." Declan barked, ashamed.
			"Thank you." the leader grinned. "So?"
			"He... he told me he'd killed 12 men, and planned to kill more. He said people had taken him, and... twisted him inside. And that they were going to do it again."
			"Anything else?"
			"No, I swear."
			Number Four pulled the hammer on his gun.
			"As God is my witness, I swear."
			"Very well." the leader grinned. "Alright boys - take aim."
			"NO! Please, shoot me if you must, but let them go!" Declan roared.
			"Oh, lookie here! A good old fashioned martyr! There's comfier ways to sainthood, Chaplain."
			The leader drew his pistol, smirking devilishly.
			He pulled back the slide, loading the round.
			Declan closed his eyes.
			He fully expected that, when they reopened, he'd be in hell.
			But there was one 'demon' that wasn't having that.

			*DING-DONG, DING-DONG. DING-DONG-DING-DONG!* the church bells rang, the noise ripping through the air.
			The Agents raised their weapons, flashlights on.
			"Come out!" the leader barked.
			A laughing noise - a guttural, demonic laughing noise cackled through the hall.
			Connor darted from rafter to rafter, his twinned windpipes flexing.
			One kept the laughing, while the other began to speak.
			"Deliver the poor and needy. Rid them out of the hand of the wicked." he recited.
			"So... you betrayed your true purpose, to become a preacher boy? Is that it?" the leader snarled.
			The laughter wouldn't stop. The other voice continued.
			"I will be merciless, and punish them in anger. And when I exact vengeance, they shall know that I am the Lord."
			The words boomed throughout the chapel, as the laughter grew more unhinged.
			"LIGHT HIM UP!" the leader roared.
			The Agents' guns erupted in a hail of fire, as bullet after bullet dug into the rafters and ceiling.
			"Cease fire! Cease fire!"
			The Agents frantically searched with their flashlights, looking for their prey.
			Declan had knee-walked over to the others - and, like true Catholics, it seemed he and Mary were competing for who would be the human shield.
			"Circle formation! Back to back! Don't let him get the drop on us!"
			The Agents quickly moved into position, searching through panicked breaths.
			In the middle of the circle, a large metal grate stood. Its purpose was to drain mopwater from the church floor, as well as provide easy maintenance access to the supply pipes.
			Humans weren't meant to fit in there. Indeed, the only real access point within the Werewolf's reach was another gutter on the upper floor, which connected to a chute that brought dirt and soap down into the wider drainage network.
			And yet... hypermobile joints, combined with a pain tolerance that thought nothing of dislocating one's shoulders...
			"The righteous shall rejoice when he seeth the vengeance!"
			At that, the grate burst open, and a red-eyed demon roared out.
			The Agents turned quickly.
			Not quickly enough.
			Connor's first strike disembowelled Number Four. The second took off Number Six's head. The third was a slice, then an impalement stab, over Number Two's chest.
			The Agent's guns roared for a split second, before uselessly clicking.
			"DAMN IT! RELOADI---" Number Five barked, before a wristblade turned his throat into set dressing.
			Connor turned quick, sending his blade upwards. It stabbed upside Number Three's head, poking out the top of his skull. A quick rip tore the head off surprisingly cleanly.
			Finally, the leader drew his machete.
			"Come get some, Traitor!"
			Connor's eyes blazed, as he charged.
			The leader's swipe slashed open his throat.
			Usually, that ends a fight.
			Oh, the fight ended, sure.
			The leader's shocked expression quickly went vacant, as Connor's blades drove into his ribcage. Then they swept out, and the gory paste that was once a Super-Agent fell to the floor.
			Connor huffed. Heaved. He pulled out his Coagulator, and quickly sprayed his neck with it.
			Then, he breathed properly again.
			"Are... are you..." Declan gasped, pale. "Are you alright?" he finally spluttered.
			"You mean, apart from the unwanted tracheotomy?" Connor would've quipped. Instead, he let out a rasp, before sighing - well, "sighing," and putting a thumb up.
			"I... I'm sorry, I... I'm so sorry." Declan cried.
			Connor put a gentle hand on Declan's shoulder, then patted it. He turned, and saw Mary and Danny looking up at him.
			Mary was pale as a sheet. All her knowledge of theology couldn't prepare her for this.
			Danny, however, looked up in awe.
			"Are you... Azrael?" he asked.
			Connor chuckled. The Angel of Death. Incidentally, not recognised as such by the Catholic church - Danny was a heretic in the making, it seemed.
			And yet, it was clear the child meant no harm by it. To Danny, his saviour was a monster - a holy, righteous monster.
			Connor heaved a bloody breath, stepping forwards.
			The wounds from Pig Head's wrath had reopened in the carnage. He was supposed to be dead.
			Indeed, he walked through the valley of the shadow of death.
			No one was with him. Neither rod nor staff comforted him.
			But as his crimson eyes dimmed, and he melted into the night, he feared no evil.

But if a pipe sprung a leak, they would have to dig up the entire road to get to it - so they instead made the first tunnels for easier maintenance access--"

	EPISODE - Crusades, Unending
		______________________________
		SCENE
			Autumnal evenings in Drackhill were often grim, and tonight's, it seemed, would be no different.
			The sky gods had clearly decided to add some variety to the valley's night - you could almost feel their laughter as hail crashed down from the heavens.
			Despite this, the city still needed its monstrous heroes. No rest for the virtuous, it seemed.

			"*DIE!*" Connor screamed, delivering his wristblade right into a battered Super-Agent's heart. At the same time, Sparky's jaws tore the head off another, while a satisfying *KK-BOOM!* noise punctuated Ivan's sniper fire.
			"Command, this is Zulu 7! We're pinned down here! Need reinforcements!" one Agent barked into his radio, just before the twin Werewolves pounced on him. In moments, they reduced him to paste.

			Just outside the city, in an armoured van, sat a radio operator, hearing the screams of his Agents. The black veins around his eyes darkened with mutant adrenaline.
			"HQ, this is Command Post 8-4. Request deployment of Crusader unit."
			"HQ copies. Crusader unit en-route."

			The bullet slammed right into Connor's head, making his ears ring as he stumbled backwards.
			The shooter grinned, but not for long - Ivan's return fire made his head pop like a grape.
			"Connor! Are you okay?" Sparky asked, rushing over.

At the same time, an electric current coursed through it, which danced across his skin before jolting in, sending scorching pain straight into his neurons.
			Were Connor his usual self, he'd crack a joke about what kind of insanity must have driven the creation of this device - some bastard child of a chainsaw and a stun baton, squeezed into a machete - but instead, he howled in unimaginable fury.

			"Chyort!" he gasped, holstering Fyodor and pulling his sawn-off shotgun from his rifle. He charged forward, and delivered both barrels into the Agent's centre mass. The Agent fell backwards, dazed but otherwise unharmed.

			"Yeah, I'm on a date. She'll be here any minute." Amy replied.

Especially because it took so long for me to start speaking - all the other kids would be singing along their choirs and prayers, and I'd just be sat there. I had a bad stutter growing up, but I went to a speech therapist to 'fix' it." she explained, putting 'fix' in scare-quotes. "You've probably noticed my lisp, as well. 		Day in the life

			"Oh, Jesus, I'm so sorry." she sighed. "Those idiots... someone needs to sort them out. I mean, not like that Werewolf bastard... but someone needs to do something."
			"You're not a fan of the Werewolf?"
			"He murdered my son." she said coldly.
			"Right..." he looked away, guiltily. "Sorry."
			"Don't be. He did it, not you." she smiled. "Well, I'm glad you came. I've been meaning to show you something."
			She reached for the photo album on the side table - the same one he'd seen before. She flipped it open to a page he hadn't seen.
			Steve. A chubby toddler with a gap-toothed grin, holding a toy truck.
			"This was him at three." she said, her voice softening. "Look at those cheeks. He was always a chubby little thing. Used to call him my little dumpling."
			Connor's throat tightened. He said nothing.
			She turned the page. Steve as a schoolboy, in a uniform far too big for him. Then, as a teenager, awkward and pimply, standing next to the Renegade.
			"And this one..." she beamed, pointing at a photo of Steve on a beach, squinting into the sun.
			"This was his first proper holiday. We went to Bournemouth. He ate so much ice cream he was sick on the pier." 
			She chuckled, then coughed. "Happy memories."
			"Yeah." Connor whispered.
			He could feel her looking at him.
			"You know..." she began. "I really appreciate this. When you get to my age, you don't have anyone drop by to let you share your old stories. Even Steve didn't drop by this much."
			Connor's hands were trembling. He set the mug down before he dropped it.
			"He was a good boy," Eileen continued, her eyes still on the photo. "Mixed with the wrong crowd, sure. But deep down, he was a good boy. He just... lost his way."
			"I'm sorry." Connor whispered.
			"I've told you, stop saying that." she chuckled. "You didn't--"
			"I--I'm sorry, I can't... I can't do this."
			She tilted her head, confused. "Can't do what? Drink your tea?"
			Connor set the cup down. His whole body was shaking now. His vision blurred.
			"I can't keep lying. To you, to everyone..."
			"What? What lie?"
			He looked up at her. She'd gone as pale as he had.
			"Steve. I... I killed him."
			"Fuck." he thought. He didn't mean to blurt it out.
			Fuck. Fuck!
			The silence that followed was suffocating.
			"What?"
			Eileen's voice was barely a whisper.
			"I--I didn't mean to! He was gonna shoot me, and I--I didn't know I'd survive it, so I shot back, and..."
			"Get out."
			"Eileen, I--"
			"GET OUT!" she screamed, her voice cracking. "GET OUT OF MY HOUSE! GET OUT! GET OUT! GET OUT!"
			Connor stumbled to his feet. Tears streamed down his face. He opened his mouth to say something - anything - but no words came.
			He turned and fled.
			He made it to the front door. His hand was on the handle when he heard it.
			*Bm-bm-bm. Bm. Bm-bm.*
			Her heart.
			"Shit! Eileen?" he rushed back.
			Too late. She'd keeled over, clutching her chest. Her face was grey, and her lips were blue.
			He grabbed his phone.
			"Ambulance! I need an ambulance! She's having a heart attack!"
			He gave the address. Put the phone on speaker. Started chest compressions.
			"Stay with me. Stay with me, Eileen. Please."
			He didn't know how long he worked. It felt like hours. It felt like seconds. The paramedics arrived, and he stepped back, his hands covered in the faint impressions of her ribs.
			They worked on her. They stabilised her. They loaded her into the ambulance.
			Connor stood in the doorway, watching them drive away.
			He was still standing there when the sun began to set.
			Fuck.

			The phone rang twice before Naismith picked up.
			"Barrett."
			Connor's voice was hollow.  "The Werewolf. He'll be in Ludford Park tonight."
			A pause.
			"How do you know?"
			"I set it up." Connor closed his eyes. "He trusts me. He won't know what's coming."
			Another pause.
			"You're doing the right thing, Connor."
			Connor said nothing. He just hung up.
			He stood in the middle of the street, staring at a wall.
			He had killed a man. He had broken an old woman's heart - literally.
			Monster.
			Inhuman.
			Villain.

		It Was Me
		______________________________
		SCENE
			Connor stood by the fountain, hands shoved in his pockets, hood up. He shifted his weight from foot to foot, glancing over his shoulder every few seconds. He checked his phone. Checked it again. Checked it a third time.
			Ludford Park.
			This ruse better work.
			"Come on, Sparky." he thought. "Where are you?"
			He didn't have to wait long.
			A black mass dropped from the trees, landing with a soft thud a few feet away. Before Connor could react, a globule of gel erupted from Sparky's palm and hit the ground.
			*FWOOM-PSHH!*
			Smoke billowed out, thick and choking, swallowing the fountain and the path and everything else.
			Connor stumbled back, coughing - pretending to cough. His eyes watered on command. He let his voice shake.
			"W-what the..."
			His other windpipe flexed. Time for some ventriloquism.
			"*You.*"
			Sparky gripped his throat, raising him up.
			"GET ME A VISUAL! *NOW!*" Naismith roared.
			"W-Werewolf..." Connor stammered.
			"*SILENCE!*" he cut himself off with.
			"You're doing great!" Sparky smiled warmly.
			"You must've gone mad." Connor snarled, his voice pitched low and monstrous. "Because I know you're not a fool. And only a fool... or a MADMAN... would BETRAY ME!"
			He threw his hands up. "I didn't--I wouldn't--"
			"LIAR! You KNOW I can *smell* liars! Did you think I didn't have eyes in the police?! DID YOU THINK I WOULDN'T *KNOW?!*"
			Sparky lunged. His claws raked across Connor's face - a sharp, stinging slash that split the skin from cheekbone to jaw. Blood welled up, hot and wet.
			Connor screamed. It wasn't entirely fake.
			He stumbled backward, clutching his face, as the smoke began to dissipate.
			Then... *BANG!*
			A gunshot. Naismith, emerging from the treeline, his pistol drawn. Another shot. Another.
			Sparky snarled, fired a grapple from his wrist, and launched himself into the air. He swung up and away, disappearing over the rooftops.
			Connor collapsed to his knees, blood streaming down his face.
			"Connor! Are you alright?!" Naismith rushed over, Nina close behind.
			"He... he..." Connor stammered, his voice cracking. "He knew. He knew. He said I betrayed him--"
			"Easy, easy." Naismith holstered his weapon and helped Connor to his feet. "You're alright. You're safe."
			Connor let himself be pulled up. He let his legs shake. He let the tears come.
			They were real. He finally let the breakdown happen.
			"I need to go." he whispered.
			"No, we need to get you to a hospital---"
			"NO!" Connor screamed, sprinting off.
			"Shit..." Naismith sighed. "God damn it... how did he know?! If there's a leak..."

			The city sprawled beneath them, glittering with a million lights. Connor sat on the edge of the roof, legs dangling over the drop, dabbing at his face with his sleeve.
			The cut was gone now. Long gone.
			Sparky sat beside him, tail curled around his paws.
			"Why did we do that?" he asked quietly.
			Connor stared out at the skyline.
			"You remember what happened when I got arrested?"
			Sparky nodded.
			Connor sighed. "Naismith had questions. About me. About the Werewolf. About why I was in the wrong place at the wrong time. He didn't know, but he was starting to suspect. And with everything that's happened - me disappearing, coming back stronger, and the Werewolf only appearing after I came back... it was only a matter of time before he put the pieces together."
			"So you staged this, to throw him off?"
			Connor shrugged. "Now he thinks I'm a victim. A witness. Someone who needs protecting, not investigating. And now, he'll be worried about who could've leaked this... he'll be distracted. Off his game."
			"He seems to always be only a step behind us." Sparky pondered. "It's never long after we strike that he turns up."
			"Well, hopefully that'll change."
			Sparky was quiet for a moment.
			"I still don't fully understand this game of pretend," he finally said. "Humans... lie so much. It's like breathing."
			Connor felt guilt shoot into his chest. "Yeah. It is."
			"But..." Sparky pressed his head against Connor's shoulder. "I understand why you do it. You have to protect the pack."
			"I'm just so tired of it, Sparky." Connor's voice cracked. "Every day, I lie to someone. It's not who I am. It's never been who I am."
			Sparky nuzzled into him.
			"I know." he said softly. "But it's for the best. For now."
			Connor took a deep breath. He wiped his eyes.
			"I need to go check on Eileen." he said.
			Sparky rose with him, stretching his shoulders.
			"Do you want company?"
			"No." Connor shook his head. "This is something I have to do alone."
			Sparky nodded, bumping his head against Connor's hand.
			"I'll take care of patrol tonight. You take some time off, okay?"
			Connor managed a small smile.
			"Thanks, buddy."
			He turned, and grappled down, leaving Sparky alone on the rooftop, watching the city glitter beneath him.

		Don't Cross a Wolf
		______________________________
		SCENE
			The hospital room was small, and sterile. The only sound was the beep of the heart monitor and the soft hiss of the oxygen tank.
			Eileen lay in the bed, looking smaller than Connor remembered. The tubes in her nose made her seem fragile in a way she'd never allowed herself to be before. Her eyes were closed, but she wasn't asleep. He could tell by her heartbeat - still weak, still fraying, but steadier than it had been.
			And fading fast.
			He stood in the doorway for a long moment. Then, he knocked softly on the frame.
			"Eileen?"
			Her eyes opened. For a moment, her expression was blank. Then, it flickered.
			Connor flinched. "I... I just wanted to check on you. Make sure you were okay. I can go, if you want."
			She stared at him. The silence stretched. Then she sighed, and waved a hand weakly.
			"Sit down, then. You're making the place look untidy."
			Connor let out a breath he didn't know he'd been holding. He stepped inside and sat in the chair by her bed. It was hard plastic and uncomfortable. He didn't care.
			"I'm sorry." he said. "For... for everything. For what I said. For what happened. I didn't mean to--"
			"Stop."
			She held up a hand.
			"Just... stop."
			He did.
			Eileen took a slow, rattling breath. The oxygen tube hissed.
			"You think you gave me a heart attack?"
			"I--"
			"You must be the most big-headed little shit I've ever met." she shook her head. "I'm eighty-two years old. I've been smoking since I was fourteen. I've got COPD, for Christ's sake. You think you did this to me?"
			Connor opened his mouth. Closed it. Opened it again.
			"But I..."
			"You what? Told me the truth?" she snorted, then coughed. "Yeah. That was a shock. But it's been waiting to give out for years. You just happened to be there when it did."
			Connor stared at her. He didn't know what to say.
			"I'm still sorry." he finally managed.
			"I know." she nodded, closing her eyes for a moment. "You're a sorry little thing, aren't you?"
			He looked down at his hands.
			"Tell me what happened." she said. "The truth. All of it."
			Connor waited for a trillion years. Two seconds passed, and he finally began to speak.
			"He... He came at me with a gun. During a raid. I--I had a gun too. I didn't think. I just... pulled the trigger. It was over in seconds."
			Eileen was quiet for a long moment.
			"His mates told me it was the Werewolf. They said the Werewolf killed him."
			Connor swallowed.
			"I... well..."
			She didn't react. Not at first. She just stared at him, her expression unreadable.
			"That explains a lot." she finally said. "Explains how you heard my heart go, at least. You get off on listening to people like that?"
			"I hate it."
			"Good."
			She took another wet breath, and choked on it.
			"Did he suffer?"
			"No." he said quietly. "It was quick."
			He hesitated, and took her hand gingerly. Then he closed his eyes, and she found herself doing the same automatically.
			His mind brushed against hers as gently as it could. He passed the memory over to her.
			The moment. The brief, violent flash of the gun. The way Steve had crumpled. The way his eyes had gone glassy and still.
			A tear rolled down her weathered cheek, as he pulled back.
			"How... how did you..."
			"It's, um... a psychic thing." he shrugged awkwardly. "I'm still working that one out."
			She sat for a moment, processing it.
			"Let me see it again."
			"Eileen..."
			"Please. I want to see him again."
			Connor reached out again, and their eyes closed once more. He held the memory still, like pinning down a rowdy drunk. His eyes flashed red under his skin, as his senses re-engaged. The smell. The sounds. The tiny, little details that humans have the luxury of forgetting.
			They pulled back again.	Connor sat with her in silence for a while. Then, she spoke.
			"I want to know why you do it. Why you go after the Skinners. Why you're the Werewolf."
			"I was taken." he said. "A few months ago. By a man called the Commandant. He owns... a private army. A death squad."
			He told her everything. The torture. The experiments. The serum.
			He told her about waking up in the lab, about the pain, about the surgeries.
			He told her about the night he escaped, and about everything that had happened since.
			By the time he finished, the room was dark. The lights had dimmed automatically. Eileen's heart monitor beeped softly in the silence.
			"I know it doesn't make up for Steve." he said. "Nothing does. But I'm trying to stop them. The people who make the Skinners possible. The people who make monsters."
			Eileen was quiet for a long moment.
			"It was my fault." she finally began.
			"What do you mean?"
			"The... the gangs."
			She took a deep, laboured breath.
			"I wasn't just in a biker club. We... we did all sorts. Ran drugs. Blackmailed. Beat people up. Even... *used* people. Back then, I thought... it was dog-eat-dog. Kill or be killed."
			She sighed, the shame washing over her.
			"That's how it started. We weren't racists, not at the beginning... but enough of us tolerated it. So, I guess it makes no difference. By the time I'd split from them, the damage was done, and the Disciples were born. Without anyone standing against it, they allied with the Skinners. That's when my Steve ended up joining. Because of me."
			"You... you were in the Patriot Kings?"
			She nodded. "You know your gang history."
			"My uncle, Vince. He went toe-to-toe with the last of them, before they fully merged into the new Disciples. Said they were has-beens."
			"We are. It's... been."
			She choked again.
			"Wait. Vince? Vince Barrett?"
			"Yeah. He raised me after I came back from Ireland." Connor nodded.
			She chuckled, then laughed a little. "Oh, fate's a funny one. Did he ever tell you about the Rexton job?"
			Connor tilted his head, and she grinned.
			"This one... this was before your time. The Hoods weren't even a thing yet - hell, this was the birthplace of the Hoods. See, it was me, your uncle, and a couple other lads - I think Tommy Crane was there too, and Casale gave us the tools for the job - we ransacked a Skinner shipment. Cost them millions. That's why I got kicked out of the Kings - if they didn't, their fancy new alliance would be in jeopardy. I think that single job is the only reason the Skinners haven't broken out of Belson yet - it took them years to make the money back. I retired on a gangster's pension, while your uncle and Crane used it to set up the Hoods."
			Connor looked up at her in awe. "So, in other words, you're like, my great-auntie?"
			She giggled, and coughed. "I'm the tough old bat who taught your uncle all he knows. Funny how things work out."
			She leaned back, and took a raspy breath.
			"All this time, I thought Steve was killed in some robbery. But now, I get it. It's a war. And he picked a side."
			"That doesn't mean it's okay." Connor said softly. "For what little it's worth... I'm sorry for what I did. If I could go back, I wouldn't've done it."
			She smiled gently. "Still... knowing that he was trying to kill you, knowing he went down fighting... it sounds horrible, I know, but... it makes it easier to swallow. It... it makes it easier to forgive you."
			"You don't have to forgive me." Connor looked away, his eyes wet. "I... I need you to know that, Eileen. You're allowed to hate me. *I* hate me."
			"Oi." she cut in. "This a private self pity party, or can anyone join? I'm the one who's dying, kid."
			"I know. I'm... I'm sorry."
			"Say 'sorry' one more time, and superpowers or not, I will outlive you." she said lowly, before grinning. "Listen... I'm glad, at the end, that we both got to say our piece. I hate a dangling thread."
			"I can give you a transfusion." he blurted out. "My blood - it's what they used to make the serum. It could help you. It could--"
			"No."
			The word was firm.
			"I've lived a long life, Connor. Eighty-two years. That's more than most get."
			She looked at him, her eyes steady. "I don't want to live forever. I don't want to be a lab experiment. I just want to go quietly. It's my time."
			"But--"
			"Don't 'but' me, kid. I've earned the right to die."
			She smiled, a hint of her old spirit flickering. "What I want is for you to stay with me. Until the end. And when I'm gone, I want you to handle my affairs, like we discussed. My house, my belongings, my funeral - and most of all, my bike. Can you do that?"
			"I... I don't know if I'm the right person. I killed--"
			"That's exactly why you're the right person." she said firmly. "You owe me. You owe Steve. And you know I've got no-one else. So, if you're half the man I think you are, you'll stay. And you'll see it through."
			Connor took a deep breath.
			"Okay." he whispered. "I'll stay."
			Eileen smiled. It was a soft, tired thing, but it was real.
			"Good lad." she closed her eyes. "Now, get me a cup of tea. The stuff they give you here tastes like piss."
			Connor laughed - a raw, wet sound, halfway to a sob.
			He returned, and she had started snoring. He smiled softly, and sat with her, holding her hand.
			She let out a raspy, rattling breath.

			"So, there you have it." Connor sighed, leaning back against the pew.
			"Wow. That is... quite the story, Connor." Declan nodded. "I... I must ask, why have you told me your name?"
			"Because I'm sick of lying. I... just wanted to be honest for a bit." he admitted.
			"I understand."
			Declan hesitated for a moment.
			"I haven't taken any confessions after what happened. I... I broke the Seal. It's a grave sin."
			"A child's life was at risk. I'd be more angry if you *didn't* break that stupid rule over it."
			Declan smiled. "Still... it may have been the lesser evil, but it was still an evil, and I am sorry."
			"Ten Hail Mary's should do it." Connor grinned, leaning forwards. "How's the kid doing?"
			"Better. Despite the horror of what he saw, his faith has only strengthened. I envy that."
			"Oh, Envy? That's a big one, right?"
			"Says Mr. Wrath himself."
			The two shared a hearty chuckle.
			"You know... the Seal of the Confessional only applies if the penitent is genuinely confessing his sins before God... I, an atheist, was instead justifying what he'd done. So arguably, no rules broken."
			"It's not normally me who receives absolution in this church." Declan chuckled. "Still... thank you for that. I appreciate it."
			Declan paused.
			"You know... when it happened, I thought you were a demon."
			"Who says I'm not?"
			"Demons are evil. You are many things... but you're not evil. Also, you're corporeal."
			Connor sighed softly. "I have bad days. Times when I'm cruel."
			"We all do."
			He paused again.
			"When we first spoke, you told me you'd been twisted up inside. I assume that was no metaphor?"
			"Not by a long shot."
			Declan hesitated, before speaking again.
			"What do you think happened?"
			"I think... I think that when they shot me, I died. I think that Heaven didn't want me; and Hell had to spit me back out - but I brought some of it with me."
			He chuckled grimly. "Okay, *that* was a metaphor."
			"An understandable one." Declan stroked his chin. "The things you do... they are gruesome, yes. But I truly believe, they are needed."
			Connor hesitated, but rose.
			"If you ever need another talk like this, or if there's anything in this church that can help... you know where to find me."
			"Thanks, father."
			He stood for a moment, before heading into the rain.
			Once again, he walked through the valley of the shadow of death.
			He feared no evil.

	EPISODE - Helping Hands

		SCENE
			Morning came, then afternoon, as Connor jogged through the high street. A voice caught his ear.

			"Yeah, pretty good." Bea smiled. "I've spent my whole morning studying the British constitution - or, lack thereof."
			"Fun stuff." Connor grinned.
			"We just finished a lab session." Chloe chimed in. "Dissections, this time."
			"Gross." Bea chuckled, putting down her food. Chloe let out a giggle.

			"Oh, uh..." Bea fumbled at her pockets. "Sorry, I'm out of change!"
			"We take card." he said firmly.
			"Right." Bea nodded awkwardly. She reached for her wallet.
			Connor looked the man up and down, and his pupils constricted slightly.
			"Guys, let's go." he said hurriedly.
			"What's wrong?" Chloe asked.
			"Nothing, just... let's go."
			"Wow." the soldier scowled. "You feel like a big man, disrespecting the Army like that?"
			"You feel like a big man, shooting little kids?" he snapped back.
			"Connor!" Bea gasped.
			"What the *fuck* did you just say to me?!" the soldier barked.

			"Come on, let's go." Chloe cut in, grabbing his arm. "Now."
			Connor took a deep breath, staring into the soldier's soul. He nodded, and they moved.
			"Very brave, kid!" the soldier jeered. "Mouthing off at real men who fought for your freedoms!"
			Connor's head snapped around, but Chloe jerked his arm.
			"Don't." she said firmly. He sighed, and carried on walking. The trio came to a halt and leaned against a wall.
			"Fuckin' Tan. Fought for my chains, more like!" he hissed.
			"Okay, what's going on?" Bea asked firmly.
			Connor raised an eyebrow.
			"I've not known you for long - but you've never seemed like the type to pick fights with strangers on the street." she pressed. "What's wrong?"
			He let out a deep breath. "Sorry... sorry."
			Another deep breath, before he explained.
			"That guy's medals - one of them was the General Service Medal for Operation Flying Fox - the occupation of my hometown."
			"Oh..." Bea realised.
			He sighed. "Seeing a man in uniform cornering us isn't a happy memory even ignoring that. To me, a soldier is someone who kicks down your door, screams in your face, smashes your windows, and beats you in the chest. And he had the nerve... the fuckin' nerve to shake his little collection box in our faces and ask for money?"
			"It's the poppy appeal..." Chloe shrugged. "I mean, they do help people--"
			"They help *soldiers.*" he corrected. "Call me heartless, but they're not better than anyone else. They don't deserve their own special charity, some massive public campaign, or every single person wearing a special flower just for them."
			He let out a breath, and bowed his head. "Sorry - I don't mean to rant about it. I know you guys get it."
			"We do." Bea nodded softly. "Look, we've gotta get back to uni, but... are you gonna be okay?"
			"Yeah, why?" he tilted his head.
			"Connor... what you're describing, it... it sounds like PTSD." Chloe said gently.
			He looked away.
			"There's no shame in it." she added quietly.
			"I know." he nodded. "I don't think colonised people have a word for PTSD. I think we just call it 'normal.'"
			Bea let out a sad smile. "We'll stay out a little longer."
			"No, guys you--you have classes..." he meekly protested.
			"Doesn't matter." Chloe smiled warmly. "Come on, let's go for a walk down the park, and talk about random stuff."
			"Sounds like a plan." Bea nodded.
			Connor hesitated, but smiled back.

		Remembrance
		______________________________
		SCENE
			It had been a long, long day at the cafe. Too long. Unsurprisingly, Amy's face lit up as she saw Connor and Sparky waiting outside for her.
			"Oh my goodness!" she beamed, rushing straight over to Sparky. "Hey, buddy! How've you been all day? Did you miss me?"
			"Yeah! Today's been good. Connor's been teaching me how to read a little better!" he barked back.
			Oblivious, Amy smiled warmly. "Such a good boy..." she cooed.
			"Nice to see you too, dickhead." Connor quipped.
			"Next time, just send the dog." she snarked back. She stood, and pulled him in for a hug.

			Connor finished tinkering away at the now-fixed wristwatch on his bedroom desk, and came into the living room. There, Amy was making a fuss over Sparky, as usual.
			"Who's a good boy? Whosagoodboyyy?" she asked in a baby voice.
			"Me, so I've been told." Sparky grinned. "Can I have the bloody treat now, or what?"
			"Paw?" she asked.
			Sparky sighed, giving a very graceful paw-shake.
			"Beg?"
			He hopped up, planting his front legs on her forearm.
			"Roll over?"
			"This bacon twist better be worth it." he grumbled, obeying.
