			"Yeah, well if you remember, *I* was always Luna's favourite." she grinned.
			He laughed heartily, as did she.
			"You know..." she began. "Ever since getting him, I've noticed you've been doing better and all."
			Connor smiled. "Yeah, well... perfect excuse to get out of the house, isn't he?"
			Sparky rolled back onto his back, and was immediately attended by Amy's belly rubs.
			"How was your day, by the way?" she asked.
			"Oh, *now* you ask!" he snarked.
			"Fuck off, I don't actually care." she grinned.
			He chuckled. "Yeah, not bad. Ran into Chloe and Bea earlier."
			"Ah, nice. How are they?"
			"They're good. We, uh... we got cornered by some poppy appeal guy."
			"Oh." Amy nodded sympathetically. "You okay?"
			"Yeah. They helped me get over it." he nodded.
			"Other than that... I know you've not said much about it, but... how are you holding up with Eileen's passing?"
			He looked away. Hated that he couldn't tell her the whole story.
			"I'm okay, I guess. I'm just glad I got to be with her at the end. I've stored some of her stuff at Riverside - along with her old bike. The rest, I'm donating to charity, like she would've wanted."
			Before he could continue, his ears pricked up. His burner phone was ringing.
			"One sec." he said, rushing into his room. He answered it.
			"Hello?"
			"Hi, Connor." the other voice replied.
			"Commandant..." Connor snarled, his face going white.
			"Commandant?!" Sparky jumped up, barking and curling his lip.
			"What's wrong?" Amy asked, confused.
			"What do you want, you fucking cunt?!" Connor snapped. "Wanna show your face? Let me pay you back for what you did to me?!"
			"'Did to you?'" Amy tilted her head. "Wait..."
			"Yeah, that's not a half-bad idea." the Commandant audibly grinned. "Meet me in Belson. Marsh Road. Unit 4-7-81/P."
			"You're a dead man. You hear me?" Connor growled. "*DEAD!*"
			A drop of hot blood came from his nostrils, and the pain in his head intensified.
			"I'll tear your throat out!" Sparky added through a roar.
			"See you soon!" the Commandant laughed, cutting off the call.
			Connor turned to Sparky. "Let's go."
			"Whoa, whoa..." Amy cut in, standing in front of the door. "You're not going anywhere."
			"Amy..." Connor began, suppressing himself. "Get out of my way."
			"No fucking chance. Not until you tell me who that is, and what they did to you."
			"Connor, we don't have time for this. He could have 217! My sister!" Sparky barked.
			"Amy, I'll explain it all later, I promise. But please, let me through. It's important."
			"No way." she shook her head. "I heard you there. And I know that look in your eye. If I let you go, you'll kill them."
			"He needs killing." Connor growled lowly.
			"Tell me why." she pressed.
			"Amy..." he said through gritted teeth. "Move."
			"Or what?" she tilted her head. "You gonna make me?"
			Connor turned away.
			"Exactly. Now start talking."
			"I don't have time. I'll tell you when I get back. I swear."
			"Tell. Me. *Now.*"
			"Please, just... just drop it..." he begged, his headache pounding like a drum in his skull. "I'll tell you later. I *don't have time.* I need to go. *NOW!*"
			"No. You're telling me. There's no reason why you can't! Something's going on, and I'm your fucking sister!" she barked. "I'm sick of this! Sick of you hiding this from me! You know all about what happened to me in foster-care, but you can't trust me enough to just TELL ME!"
			He felt the pressure building up under his skin again. Like he was going to explode.
			"Just please... get outta my way." he pleaded.
			"Not. Fucking. Happening." she shook her head.
			"*GET OUT OF MY WAY!*" he roared.
			She went pale. Not just pale, but practically white. She stumbled, and fell backwards.
			He could hear her heartbeat. It was going a mile a minute. He turned, and spotted his reflection in the window.
			"Oh... f-fuck." he whispered.
			The chitinous exoskeleton had encased him once more. And his eyes glowed bright red, lighting up the room. His claws - not hands, but claws - glinted in the light, like his fingers were knives.
			He took a deep breath, and ripped the covering from his face.
			"Amy, I--" he stammered.
			She didn't speak. Instead, she struggled to her feet, refusing to turn her back to him.
			"I... I'll let you go, just... p-please don't... don't hurt me..." she begged, tears streaming down her face.
			"Amy, I'm not gonna hurt you." he said as softly as he could. She made her way to her room, and rushed in, bolting the door.
			"Amy, wait!" he begged.
			"CONNOR!" Sparky barked, similarly encased in his battle-form. "We have to go!"
			Connor sighed, but nodded. The twin Werewolves headed out.

		Commandant Calls
		______________________________
		SCENE
			Across the city, Connor and Sparky perched atop an industrial unit. Sparky's fur flowed in the cold breeze, and their eyes flashed red as they scanned the fourth unit below.
			"Electromagnetic signals." Sparky noted. "Some electrical equipment in the walls."
			"Probably just wiring. Though, I'm not sure - that there looks like a radio receiver." Connor pointed.
			"Smells like WiFi." Sparky shrugged. "I doubt it's anything important. Can you get that plastic smell?"
			"Plastic? I thought it was oil." Connor tilted his head. "Well, this place is an industrial unit. Probably just old product."
			Sparky nodded, then his eyes darted. "See that?"
			"Yeah - cluster of heartbeats."
			He flexed his throat and unhinged his jaw, as did his packmate. They both let out an ethereal, alien song - one high-pitched enough that the bats in Wyrmrock went crazy.
			"Canines." he nodded. "A couple of them. A humanoid, too - must be the Commandant."
			"217 must be in there. She *has* to be. As for the other... they must be another sibling. More of my people."
			Connor gently stroked him between the ears.
			"This is the big moment. We get our revenge, and you get your sister back. After that... we hunt the rest of them down."
			"No time to dawdle, then." Sparky smiled. The two rose, and stretched their legs out.
			Connor closed his eyes, and focused. He flexed his thighs and calves, and felt his hot blood rush to them, saturating them with mutant power.
			Whatever the Commandant had done to him... it was going to be his undoing.
			The two rushed forward, and jumped. Their legs kicked into the roof's edge, smashing the metal downwards as they launched upwards. They landed on a skylight, crashing down.
			They landed on the ground, their arrival punctuated by raining shards of glass. 
			"COMMANDANT!" Connor roared. "SHOW YOURSELF!"
			His scream echoed in the cold, metal unit. He was answered by the sound of scraping, as a Super-Agent walked out from a storage crate, wielding twin machetes and clad in thick kevlar armour. 
			A television screen, which hanged from the wall, flashed to life. The Commandant's image flickered onto the screen.
			"Good evening, freaks." he grinned sadistically.
			"YOU FUCKING COWARD!" Connor howled. "SHOW YOUR FACE AND *DIE LIKE A MAN!*"
			"It's cute, honestly. You think you two little shits could kill me." he laughed. "And honestly, I think I may have tortured you a little too well. I tell you I'm somewhere, and mere minutes later you come running? You must miss me."
			"WHERE'S 217? WHERE'S MY SISTER?!" Sparky roared.
			"Oh, Six! Good to see you again." the Commandant smirked.
			At that, the Agent was joined by a pair of snarling, muscular mastiffs. It was barely visible past their fur, but the smell of their blood confirmed it - there was super-serum in their black veins.
			"She's not here, but don't worry - you have company. Project Fenrir wasn't a *complete* failure - that blood we harvested was given to these... mangy, rabid mutts."
			The twin Werewolves assumed a fighting stance.
			"You take the dogs - don't kill them." Connor whispered firmly, morphing blades from his wrists. "I'll fight the Agent."
			"Save some for me." Sparky snarled back, eyes burning red.
			"Sic 'em, boys!" the Commandant barked. "Agent Weiss - kill him."

			Connor wasn't here to fool around - he was here for blood. He spun forwards like a vengeful tornado, his wristblades ripping through the air. Weiss darted back, then knelt down and crossed his machetes, catching Connor's right.
			Under his mask, Connor grinned. His left blade burst forwards, aimed straight for Weiss's gut.
			Not fast enough. Weiss turned, twisting his blades so Connor's fell forward, and then he countered. Connor bent sideways into an L-shape, dodging the first machete. The second nicked his neck.
			First blood. Connor felt the wound close up in moments, and snarled viciously.
			He roared, charging forwards again.

			At first, Sparky's wolven form intimidated the lesser canids. But then both remembered what the Commandant would do if they failed, and their black-veined eyes darkened with furor.
			"Listen to me! I don't want to hurt you!" he pleaded, as he slammed the backside of his paw around the head of one. He was careful not to catch it with his claws.
			The other used the opening to sink his teeth into Sparky's back leg, tearing hot blood and red meat.
			He howled in shock and pain, before turning and beating that one down. It got back up in short order.
			Sparky turned his head, and saw Connor's fight. His pupils shrank as they caught the Commandant's image.

			"DIE!" Connor demanded, as the tip of his blade sank into Weiss's thigh.
			Most men - hell, most Super-Agents - would've been thrown off by that. Weiss simply used his proximity to drive his own blade through Connor's hand.
			Connor screamed as the blade shunted in between his carpal bones, popping out of his palm. Weiss pulled the blade backwards, splitting his hand in two.
			He flipped, and clutched his hand tight, setting the bones back and morphing a bandage to bind them. His eyes flashed crimson, and he formed bucklers over his wristblades.
			"Ah, finally - you've figured out you're not invincible, eh?" the Commandant taunted. "In fact, I'd say you're quite vincible."
			"Fuck you." Connor spat, his armour thickening and calcifying. He raced forwards, and the two monsters - one in form, one in soul - clashed again.

			Sparky snarled as another chunk of flesh tore out from his hide. He turned, and bit the scruff of the one who did it. He raised up on his hind legs, and threw it across the unit.
			Breathing space. He pounced on the other forcing it to its back.
			For normal canines, that would be it. The loser would submit, accepting that the winner would have its throat otherwise.
			The super-mastiff went right for Sparky's throat, instead. Sparky darted back just in time.
			"Please! Stop fighting me! I'm on your side! I want to stop the Commandant!" he begged.
			No answer. This wasn't one of his people - just an animal. A raging, monstrous animal.
			Sparky closed his scarlet eyes for a second.
			"I'm sorry." he whispered, as he ripped out its throat.
			He turned, as the other was sprinting towards him. He bowed his head in shame, and went for the kill.

			Connor snarled as Weiss's machete was knocked backwards by his buckler. He saw his opening and pounced forwards, paying him back in kind with a slash across the chest.
			Weiss's armour was shredded and torn, and his skin was raked and bloody - but he wasn't beaten. Not yet.
			He brought his blades together, holding them side-by-side. He half-closed his eyes, and breathed out slowly.
			Connor charged, pointing his own blades forward. He was going to impale this son of a bitch.
			Weiss held position. He felt his heart beat with anticipation. Then, he struck.
			Connor was tired. Exhausted, even. So exhausted, his reflexes were a nanosecond too late.
			Weiss's blades swept in a horizontal motion, clashing into Connor's forearms. The bucklers absorbed the damage, bending and cracking as his arms swung outwards.
			Connor went to close the opening, to put his guard back up, to do *something.*
			Too late.
			Weiss twisted his blades to their sides, and drove them through a gap in Connor's ribs.
			They sank through his armour, then his upper lungs, and punched out through his back.
			Connor went to scream - instead, blood poured from his mouth and nose, as he gurgled in pain.
			Weiss gripped the hilts of his blades, and pushed Connor to his knees.
			"Hah..." the Commandant chuckled. "I expected more. Goodbye, Connor."
			Weiss placed his foot against Connor's sternum, and pulled his blades free - slowly. Grinning.
			The blades glinted in the dim light, as he crossed them - holing them like shears ready to take the Werewolf's head.
			The blades tore through the air, sailing inward.
			Their impact sent a shock through the air, as they crashed into Connor's swiftly-raised forearms.
			"No..." he gurgled. "NO!"
			Weiss struggled, but couldn't break past the Werewolf's determined guard.
			Connor was a lot of things. A lot more, lately.
			He was not someone who knew when to die.
			"GRAAAAGH!" Sparky howled, slamming into Weiss's side. He skidded to a halt as Weiss crashed into a wall.
			Connor spat a globule of blood, and forced himself to rise.
			Weiss planted his blades in the ground, using their support to get back up. He looked at the dead mastiffs, and laughed cruelly.
			"Oh dear, Six. It's not the first time you've seen your misbegotten kind die, is it? First time you've killed them, though." the Commandant chimed in.
			"You killed them. We just put them out of their misery." Sparky snarled grimly.
			"And if you wanna see 'killing,' then we're happy to oblige." Connor added. He readied his blades, as his lungs scabbed over.
			Weiss gripped the hilts tightly, as his eyes frantically darted side to side.
			The Werewolves charged in.
			Sparky hit first. Weiss's blade cut across his muzzle, but the crimson-eyed beast was unfazed. His teeth sank into Weiss's side, ripping out chunks of hot meat.
			Connor, meanwhile, sent his own blades down - ripping off Weiss's right hand. He screamed in pain, but then Sparky's claws sank into his throat.
			Connor grabbed the fallen machete, and swept as hard as he could.
			Weiss's body fell to the ground. His head landed a few feet away.
			"Credit where it's due." the Commandant grinned. "The data we've gained from this encounter is... invaluable."
			Sparky's hackles rose.
			Connor didn't move. His blades stayed forward, tense. "We're coming for you. We're going to make you feel everything you did to us. But before we do - where's 217?"
			The Commandant tilted his head, as if considering it. "Still on that, huh?"
			A faint crackle ran through the walls.
			Connor noticed it first. Not heard - felt. A low, irregular pulse under the metal floor. His eyes narrowed.
			"Well, now." the Commandant grinned. "Isn't this a nice trip down memory lane?"
			Connor's stare tightened. "What did you do?"
			"Not the first time Six has watched his kind die because of me. And definitely not the first time you've been buried."
			Connor went still. He tilted his head, but then, his irises shrank to pinpoints. His twin heartbeats turned to hums of terror.
			"Ah... the penny drops."
			Sparky's red gaze darted to his packmate. "Connor...?"
			"RUN!" he screamed.
			"What?! Why?!"
			"PLASTIC! IN THE WALLS!"
			Too late.
			The sound came first: a deep, mechanical *thump* from inside the walls.
			Then heat.
			The world around him erupted into flame. A massive explosion shook the building, and down it came.

			Sparky pulled himself out of the wreckage first. He frantically started digging, cutting his paw pads apart on the shrapnel. Finally, he unearthed Connor, who took a sharp intake of breath.
			The ringing in his ears was deafening. His vision blurred as he came to, the world around him a hazy mess of rubble and smoke. He groaned, disoriented, but alive.
			"Connor! Come on, we've got to go! The police will be here soon!"
			The sound of sirens wailing in the distance cut through the haze. Connor tried to rise, but looked back in horror. His hand was pinned under an entire wall's worth of rubble.
			His hearts raced as panic set in. He tugged at the debris, his breath coming in sharp gasps, but his hand remained firmly caught.
			"No... no, no, no..." he stuttered.
			He shifted his weight, tried to use his enhanced strength, but it was useless. His hand was trapped, and couldn't leave unless he freed it.
			Sparky put all his might into shifting the mess, but he could barely budge it.
			"Connor, I... I'm not strong enough." he cried.
			A grim realisation dawned on him.
			He morphed a serrated dagger from his free hand. The blade's edge gleamed under the light. He gritted his teeth and pressed it into his trapped forearm.
			Squelch.
			*SHK!*
			The world slowed. The pain was like nothing he'd ever felt before - sharp, intense, and relentless.
			It coursed through him, amplifying every sensation, turning his vision dark at the edges.
			Squelch again.
			*SHK-SHK!*
			The flesh had been severed. Only bone left - too strong for even his knife to saw through.
			He grimaced, pale as a ghost, and his stomach heaved.
			*HAWK-ptoo!*
			The bone hissed as the acid bit through it. After a while, it was weak enough.
			*SHK-SHK!*
			*SHHK!*
			*SNAP.*
			With a final, brutal motion, he freed himself, his body recoiling from the sheer agony of it all. As he pulled free, the flesh ripped, and his wrist-joint popped.
			He rose to his feet, breathless, bloodied, and battered.
			The world slowed down to a standstill. If normal pain could sharpen a mind - what could this pain do?
			He tensed, squeezing his eyes shut. Despite his eyelids being closed, his irises glowed with such a bright, brilliant red, that they shone past the skin. The glow faded, and the bleeding finally stopped. A bark from Sparky shook him from his stupor, and the pair sprinted up a wall back to their overlook, just as police and fire engines poured onto the site.

		The Loss of a Hand
		______________________________
		SCENE
			It had been a hundred years. It had been a couple of seconds.
			Connor woke up on the roof. As he did, Sparky rushed over, and licked his face frantically.
			"Are you okay?" he asked, worried.
			"Hah... I'm fine. Just blacked out for a moment." he nodded, his head feeling both light and heavy.
			He morphed back down into his civilian clothes, and reached into his pocket. He pulled out a small pack of cigarettes.
			"Thank god these weren't squished back there." he chuckled, holding one in his mouth, and lighting it. The motion was tricky with one hand, but he managed.
			"Why do you burn those stinky sticks?" Sparky asked.
			"Honestly? Not much use to me these days. Downside of being a super-powered mutant is you can't get anything out of nicotine." he shrugged. "Still, the ritual of it... calms me down, I guess."
			Sparky nodded, and sat down with his packmate. "What happens now?" he asked.
			"Now? Now we see if I can grow back limbs." Connor laughed and coughed. "If I can't... we may need to rethink our operation."
			He leant back. "I've been putting off asking you... maybe because I'm scared about what you'll say. But... this whole thing with the Commandant..."
			"He was... he was right." Sparky said, nearly gagging on the words. "We thought we were better, but all it took was one phone call, and it's like we're back in the cages again."
			Connor looked away for a minute, before turning back.
			"My memories of it all... they're jumbled. I can't remember us escaping the first time. But... you remember, don't you?"
			Sparky thought for a moment.
			"All my life, I remember being in this cage. Being hurt by the bad men." he began. "And none of them ever cared. They just kept hurting me. Sometimes it was for fun, sometimes I think they were being curious, but it was always cruel. And..." he paused. "And then, one day, the bad men brought you in. You were hurt, badly - but alive. They chained you up. I wasn't in the room, but I could hear you screaming as they hurt you too."
			Connor leant forward, listening intently.
			"I kept hearing them talking about programming. I think they wanted to train you. They kept saying these specific words - 'Listen and Obey.'"
			Connor flinched at the words. Even hearing them telepathically from a wolf didn't soften their blow.
			"Every time they did, they hurt you." Sparky continued. "One day, your screaming was louder than ever before. I heard you thrashing and smashing about, and you burst out of the door they held you in. You came running out, and I knew you were different. You looked at me, and I didn't see cruelty, just sadness. I begged you to let me out, and you heard me, and you saved me."
			Connor rubbed his temples with his intact hand, processing. "So... we broke out, together?"
			"Yes. We ran for miles and miles." Sparky nodded. "But they caught up to us. They overwhelmed us, and dragged us away. They separated us - I never knew what happened to you afterwards."
			Connor looked downwards. "And... they brought you back to the place I found you?"
			"No. They brought me back to where we first met." Sparky explained. "But they were worried you might come back for me. So they moved me to the other place - the one where you and Ivan saved me."
			Connor leaned back. "Did, um... did you ever see me leave on my own? The Commandant... he pulled a trick on me."
			"No, never." Sparky shook his head.
			Connor stroked his chin. "Makes sense. We escape together, then after they bring us both back, the Commandant stages another escape to crush my hopes of leaving. They must've somehow wiped my memories of us getting out, too."
			Sparky looked away. "They were cruel. After meeting so many normal humans, I don't get it. Humans aren't so different to wolves. You're naturally decent. So what's wrong with them?"
			Connor sighed. "I don't know, bud. They're cruel. Evil. Monsters..."
			Sparky thought for a moment. "The word he used - Fenrir. That's what they called me, too."
			"Project Fenrir... that explains the super-dogs earlier." Connor nodded, visibly joining the dots. "Whatever made me and the Super-Agents, Fenrir made you and the dogs."
			"They're building an army." Sparky realised in horror.
			"Still... it doesn't explain why we're different. I mean, you couldn't hear the dogs talking, could you?"
			"No, nothing." Sparky shook his head. "This weird connection we have... I think it's just us."

			Connor paused. He closed his eyes, hesitated, and reached out. He placed his hand on Sparky's head, and their minds touched.
			Fear. Pain. Rage. All swirling through his mind, like he was pulling the depths of the ocean to the surface. He reached inwards, and Sparky let him in.
			This 'mind-bond' they had was utterly alien to both. The flashes, the shared dreams... and now this. Connor stretched his mind's eye into Sparky's subconsciousness, and watched. He saw himself, bursting out of a steel door, drenched in blood and howling in pain. He felt Sparky's memories, his emotions, his senses... the link grew stronger. Sparky saw through Connor's eyes, and Connor through Sparky's. The line where one ended and the other began had blurred into oblivion.
			Connor saw the torment Sparky had faced. Horrific surgeries. Agonising tests. He watched as the rest of Sparky's litter died, until only he was left.
			Sparky saw Connor's own pain. The torments. And others, too. He saw the moment Vince was arrested. He saw the days in the Bogside where Connor's grandfather beat him. He saw a blazing inferno in a car, with his grandmother's burning corpse hanging out. And deeper still, he watched through Connor's eyes as drove a fire poker through an older man's head.
			It was too much. The two pulled back, and rubbed their skulls, regaining their senses of self. After a short while, they both opened their eyes, and looked down - as though visibly checking which one they were.
			"You okay?" Connor asked.
			"Yeah, I... I'm Sparky, right?" he replied.
			"Yeah. Which means I'm Connor... alright, I'm okay now."
			"Me and 217 did that once. It feels like we became one person for a moment."
			"I did the same thing with Nabira the other day." Connor nodded, and closed his eyes again.
			"Who was that man?" Sparky asked.
			"Which one?"
			"The one you stabbed. I felt that memory..."
			Connor sighed. "James Laverty." he finally said, half-spitting the name. "He... he was mine and Amy's foster-carer."
			"What's a foster-carer?
			"They're supposed to be caregivers. A bit like what I am to you. Someone who isn't your parent, but raises you anyway. But he... he was a monster."
			Worse, deeper memories washed into Connor's mind. Flashes of Laverty... and what he did to Amy. He reached his hand back out, and rejoined his mind with Sparky.
			Sparky took in the flashes, then pulled his head back in disgust.
			"Good work." he nodded. "But you were a pup back then?"
			"Yeah, it was before I got my powers." Connor shrugged. "I don't know how, I just... I went berserk. After that, I was taken away by the police. Thankfully, they decided not to press charges, and that's how me and Amy came to live with Vince."
			Connor sighed. He recalled the memories he'd gleaned from Sparky.
			"I saw your memories too, you know. You... you survived all of that."
			Sparky jumped up, and rested his head on Connor's lap. "You did too. Until I met you, I never knew humans could be nice."
			"You've always been so good with people though." Connor replied. "When Amy came back on your first night with us, you were so good with her. And you were just as good with our other friends."
			"I guess... it's because I had you." Sparky mused. "You saved me from that place. So, I trust you. And that means, I trust who you trust."
			Connor smiled warmly. "I trust you too."
			He went to stroke Sparky's head, before realising he was using the wrong arm. He chuckled grimly.
			"We've both been through hell." he began. "And that's not gonna heal any time soon. But we have each other. Before I had you, I was... I was a wreck. I wanted to die, because the pain was too much. But then you came along. And you were the only creature on Earth who could know what I was going through. More than that, you needed me as much as I needed you. So looking after you... helps me."
			"What do you mean?" Sparky tilted his head.
			"I mean, when it was just me, I could let myself fall apart. But with you here, I have to stick around to help you. Not only that, when you're suffering, I've gotta do something. I can justify not helping myself - I can't justify not helping you. And through that, I learned to help myself. Through being kind to you, I learned to be kind to myself. Through helping absolve you, I... I found my own absolution."
			Sparky nuzzled his face into Connor's chest.
			"You're right. We're the only things like us. Which means we can get through this pain... together."

			At the same time, Naismith was overlooking the smouldering ruins. Nina approached him.
			"Good news, sir. We were able to shift the wreckage. We've recovered the hand." she said.
			"In what condition?" Naismith asked.
			"Pristine, sir." she replied. "I've already called the FIs to prep for immediate analysis. Though it's missing a lot of bone, they should still be able to extract prints and DNA."
			"Missing bone?" Naismith tilted his head.
			Nina nodded. "I'm no FI, but it looked to me as though he'd cut the flesh around the bone, and then just pulled until the wrist popped off. As a result, there's the flesh from the wrist, but no forearm-bone. Well, either that, or he doesn't have forearm bones." she chuckled.
			Naismith smirked. "The man's a bloody alien, I'll tell ya."
			As he said this, the hand was brought past them in a container. Nina yelped, as did an FI - the hand was *twitching.*
			"Jesus..." Naismith muttered. "What the fuck?"
			"The techs will have a field day, sir." Nina nodded, shuddering.
			"Well then." Naismith smiled. "Let's get to work."

		Trauma-dumping
		______________________________
		SCENE
			It was past midnight now. Connor had been dreading this, but it needed to be done.
			He opened his flat's door.
			Immediately, his eyes flashed red for a second. He saw Amy's heartbeat behind her door.
			She was sat against it, as if barricading herself away.
			Timidly, he approached. He could hear her breathing quicken as he walked, and her heart skip a beat as he knocked.
			"Amy..." he whispered. "It's... it's me. Connor."
			She didn't say anything. She just silently sobbed, covering her mouth so as not to scream.
			He sat down against her door. Even without super-senses, she could feel her brother's presence opposite her.
			Connor sighed. "These... these men, they shot me in the head. They took me away, and they... did something to me. Experimented on me. Tortured me. Made me into... this."
			Her breathing trembled.
			"I wanted to tell you..." he continued, his voice cracking. "I... I was just scared. Scared it might put a target on your back, scared you'd think I was crazy, scared I *was* crazy... and scared that I'd scare you. Like now."
			She sniffled softly, clutching her knees.
			"I know it's a lot... I can't imagine how you are right now, but I..." he began, tears rolling down his face. "I could really use my sister right now."
			She took a deep breath, stood, and opened the door. He rose too.
			She wordlessly pulled him in for an embrace. He held his arms out awkwardly, before wrapping her in them. They both took a moment to breathe.

			Finally, she pulled back, and looked at him, before going pale again.
			"Uh... what the hell?! What happened? W-where the fuck is your hand?!" she stammered, horrified.
			"Oh, shit." Connor sighed, sitting her down.
			"What happened?!" she repeated. Sparky jumped up, and curled into a ball next to her. She absently stroked his fur, grounding herself.
			"I got pinned under some rubble." Connor explained nonchalantly.
			"You... you cut off your own hand?" she asked.
			"...yes." he nodded. "It was either that, or get caught by the police."
			"Can you grow hands back? Is that one of your superpowers?"
			Connor allowed himself a chuckle. "Superpowers?"
			"You *do* know I saw you at the Horse, right? Getting shot in the chest six times and barely flinching?" she cocked an eyebrow.
			"Fair enough." he grinned. "Anyway, I'm not sure. Never lost a limb before. But..." he began, pulling up his sleeve. "It's healed a little. Look at the bone - there was more sticking out earlier. Hell, my wrist-bone seems to be growing back too."
			He pointed at the stump, revealing a fledgling wrist-joint forming above his arm-bone. His skin and flesh was creeping up the bone, covering it neatly. He hadn't looked at it in the light, but now he could see - His bone was dark, as though someone mixed calcium with coal. His brain flashed back to his school chemistry lessons, but he shook his head.
			"Plus, I've grown back teeth before, and I've healed away scars." he shrugged.
			Amy gulped, and held his stump gently.
			"So... you're gonna be okay?" she asked finally.
			"Probably. If not, I'm sure I can get some decent prosthetics from the KGB." he answered nonchalantly.
			"The KGB?" she cocked her eyebrow.
			"Long story. But yeah, the KGB are helping me. Whoever these freaks I'm fighting are, they're clearly connected to fascists - and for all their faults, the KGB *hate* fascism."
			Amy nodded slightly, then allowed herself a chuckle. "Christ, if Vince knew you were working with communists, he'd be jumping for joy."
			Connor laughed. "Just wait 'til we get the IRA on-side."
			She giggled, then went quiet. "So... you're the Werewolf?"
			"I have *no* idea where that nickname comes from." Connor chuckled grimly. Amy allowed herself a laugh.
			"Yeah. It's fucking lame." she snarked, still in shock.
			"So... you snitched to the police... on yourself?"
			"It was a ruse." Connor shrugged. "They were getting good at catching me. I screwed up when I went after Trey's attackers, but I managed to spin it around."
			"You learn that in the KGB?"
			"I'm not a spy." he grinned.
			"No, just a superhero." she snarked.

			She paused, hesitant. "You... you mentioned torture?"
			Connor sighed, and nodded. "The Commandant - the guy who phoned earlier. He put me through hell."
			"Why? Why would he do that?"
			"Not sure yet. But either way, he kidnapped me, tortured me, and changed me."
			He took a deep breath, before continuing.
			"It wasn't just physical. I mean, they cut me up, zapped me, put me in an ice bath, waterboarded me, you name it. But the worst was the tricks."
			"Tricks?"
			"One time, he let me think I was escaping. Just as I was about to leave, he shot me, and brought me back in. Not only that, they fucked with my head somehow... the memories are jumbled."
			"So how did you escape? How did you come back home?"
			"I snapped." he shuddered. "The Commandant was gone, and there was some other goon stood with me. I bit his throat out, and... ate him."
			"*Ate him?!*" she gasped.
			"I... it's not how it sounds. I'd been starved, and I was half-feral." he quickly explained.
			"I-I'm not judging you." she quickly corrected. "You did what you had to do, I'm sure of it. Just... a lot to process."
			He nodded, and swallowed, as if forcing the memories back down.
			"Anyway... after that, the whole place got blown up. I was buried then, too - didn't have to cut my hand off, though. Instead, I got burned to a crisp. Managed to dig my way out, and... ended up back here. The rest, I suppose you know."
			She nodded. "And... now, he's dead?"
			"No. This was just a trap. He's... he's still out there." he shook his head. His voice slowly turned to a growl.

			Amy paused, taking it all in.
			"I... thanks for telling me. And... I get why you didn't."
			He smiled sadly.
			"Does anyone else know?" she asked. "Besides, you know... the *KGB?*"
			"Tommy knows." Connor admitted. "You remember Reece Tomlinson?"
			"Stoker's goon? The one who got his head shot off?" she tilted her head. "He was one of the cunts who came at me in Raj's."
			"I killed him." Connor sighed. "I didn't mean to. He came for me shortly after I escaped, and I hit him in the chin."
			"His head had been blown off with a shotgun!" Amy countered.
			Connor sighed. "I'm *that* strong. When fighting humans, it's like their skin is paper and their bones are glass. It's taken me a hell of a lot of effort to avoid killing them by accident."
			"Humans?" she interjected, head tilted.
			Connor sighed again. "I'm not human anymore. Whatever they did to me... it's safe to say, I'm post-human. As are the people I kill."
			"So those rumours about the Skinners..."
			"All true. The people I'm hunting have this weird drug... it makes people stronger, faster, tougher, you name it. For some reason, I'm tougher than most who take it. Still working that one out."
			Amy shook her head. "I thought I recognised that look on your face."
			"Hm?"
			"When you first came to mine, after you went missing." she explained. "You had a look on your face - like shellshock. You looked the exact same way when... when you killed Laverty."
			Connor tensed up a little. "Yeah, I suppose I did. Guess I was always a killer, then, eh?"
			"No." she said firmly. "You killed him to save me. Same as the other freaks you've taken out - you killed them to save other people."
			Connor took a deep breath, and nodded. "Yeah, I... I suppose. I definitely don't regret killing *him.*"

			"Anything else I need to know? Can you fly or something? Laser eyes? X-ray vision?" she quipped.
			"Super-senses." he nonchalantly shrugged. "Strength, endurance, stamina... you've seen the shapeshifting, too. I've no idea how it all works. Oh, and Sparky can talk."

			"Remember the night I brought him back?"

			"Hah, good point! I can prove it, if you like - ask me to do something too complicated for a dog to have been trained to do, and I'll do it." Connor relayed this too, and Amy thought for a moment.
			"Okay... take the number 5, and take away 3, then add 7. Don't say the answer, just bark until you've barked the exact number of times the answer is." Amy said, folding her arms sceptically, not expecting Sparky to pass this test. Immediately though, Sparky barked nine times, and then smiled.
			"Wait, that's... holy shit. You... you can understand?! You're... you're a person?!" she said, amazed.
			"Yes! You believe me! Hello!" Sparky replied excitedly.
			"Holy hell..." Amy responded, awestruck. "We have a talking dog. Amazing..."
			"I'm sorry I didn't tell you sooner..." Connor said shyly.
			"Don't be." Amy smiled. "I... I understand why something like this would need to be secret. Which is why you can't tell anyone else."
			"Amy?" Connor asked, raising an eyebrow.

			"You're right... telling more people just creates more targets for them to go after." Connor mused.
			"Exactly." Amy nodded. "And it increases the chance that someone will slip up. I'm so, so glad you told me - but I'm not going to tell anyone. And I'm begging you not to tell another soul about this, until the whole thing is sorted."
			"You're right." Connor agreed.
			"That includes Chloe." Amy said firmly.
			"Wh-why would I tell Chloe?" Connor asked shyly.

Having loads of small ones makes that process easier."

		Pre-Whiplash

			"Thanks, doc." Connor bowed his head. "I owe you one."
			"Not even slightly." she smiled. "Although, that haemostatic foam gun - I'd love to get a few for the trauma department."
			"Somehow, I doubt I'd get manufacturer's certification." Connor grinned. "Still, I'll cobble one for you to keep on the DL."
			He motioned, and Whiplash rose. She limped as the pair left Judi's living room-turned-clinic.

			"Why'd you save me?" she asked.
			Connor paused, folding his arms.
			"Three reasons. First, because I wanna know some things. Second... well, you're not with Paladin, so there's no inherent reason to kill you. Third... you were in a lot of pain. And I could help."
			"Oh, don't tell me you've fallen for me." she grinned.
			"I do that." he sighed. "Masking. I do it all the time. I quip during fights, I banter with my friends, I--"
			"Spare me the psychoanalysis." she cut in harshly. "What's the real reason?"
			"I've just given three."
			"Three bullshit reasons." she scoffed. "You wouldn't save me unless there was something in it for you. Something more than a little chat."
			"Is it that hard to believe I would help you?" he tilted his head.
			"Yes." she nodded curtly. "I tried to kill you."
			Connor sighed again. "You know, one guy shot at me with a sniper rifle. Then he unloaded a shotgun into my chest. He's now one of my closest allies."
			"'Allies?' Are you asking me on a date?" she snarked.
			"I'm guessing the guys who paid you won't be too happy." he shrugged. "And I'm guessing someone with your... 'talents...' would be a lot of trouble for them to go after. Why not work together?"
			She looked away. "No. It's too dangerous."
			"Whiplash." he said firmly. "I can see in slow motion, so I saw what you can do."
			She sighed, leaning back. "It's called Trajectory Manipulation. A form of telekinesis."
			"How do you do it?"
			"How do you turn yourself into a smoke bomb and shit knives out of your hands?" she chuckled, before pausing. "I... I was only a little girl when they took me."
			Connor nodded, wordlessly encouraging her. She hesitated, and folded her arms - as if putting up a shield.
			"They put you in this airtight pod, filled with lukewarm water, and they whack an oxygen mask on your face." she continued. Her eyes squeezed shut, as if she was back in the pod once again. "You can't hear, smell, taste, feel, see... complete sensory deprivation."
			"How long do you stay in?" he asked.
			"As long as it takes." she shuddered. "They let you out once you manage to tell them the password. And the only way to get the password... is to read someone's mind."
			"How do you do that?"
			"That's what the deprivation is for." she nodded. "If your five senses are shut off, you're forced to rely on your sixth. That's why they lock up kids - apparently, children's myelin sheaths are less developed, which makes them more receptive to... to that kind of training."
			"And once your sixth sense is activated... you're what, a psychic?"
			"Esper. That was the term they used." she shrugged. "You still need to be trained, though. Most of our 'powers' are far too complicated to use right off the bat. For example, I can manipulate trajectories, but I never trained in general telekinesis. For my... line of work... you need a more subtle touch."
			"Am I an 'Esper?'" he tilted his head. "I can do this... weird mind-merge thingy."
			She stroked her chin. "Describe it to me."
			"Well, I can understand what my dog is saying." he nonchalantly shrugged. "He's got the same powers as me. Also, if I'm touching someone, I can understand them, no matter what language they speak - and vice versa, too. I can also read people's emotions - and tell if they're lying. I've even... even managed to see into their memories - and them into mine. Like we become one person for a moment."
			"Tactile telepathy." she nodded. "That's one of the first things they teach you. Makes sense - if you've never been trained, that's probably the only thing you'd be able to do off the bat."
			Connor cleared his throat. "So, this... psychic laboratory, or whatever - who are they?"
			"ODIN." she shrugged. "Operational Directorate for Investigative Neurokinetics. They were originally a CIA black project called MKULTRA; when they realised they were *actually* on to something, they went solo."
			"ODIN... they really squeezed to make that acronym fit, eh?" he snarked.
			She let out a soft laugh. "You're telling me. What with us, PaladinCorp, and Eidolon - you have a habit of getting people with ominous names to try and kill you."
			"So, ODIN - they're the ones who want me dead?"
			"No. They produce assassins. The man who *hired* me wants you dead." she chuckled grimly.
			"And who's that?"
			"I'm not sure." she sighed. "He's some rich man, by the looks of it. I don't get hired to ask questions."
			"Did he mention the *why,* at least?"
			"He gave me a dossier." she admitted. "You killing Hattab was highlighted. That, and your kill count on Super-Agents."
			"What's yours?"
			She hesitated. "103 Super-Agents and fellow Espers. And... 12 humans."
			"And when you say 'rouge elements...'"
			"Paladin mercs and ODIN operatives who deserted." she nodded. "Our creators don't want the general public knowing about superhumans. Your playing the hero is what made them hire me."
			"Well, if your employer has a problem, I'd love for him to lodge a complaint in person..." Connor savagely grinned.
			She chuckled, before pausing. "He'll be after me, now. And so will they..."
			"Why would they come after you?"
			"Because I failed." she admitted, choking up a little - not out of shame, but fear. "I know the punishment for failing and not dying. I've seen it delivered."
			"Then stay here." he said softly. "If they come here, we can fight them off together."
			She looked at him, her eyes trembling slightly. "I... I can't. I've got to go off the grid - at least for a while."
			"I get it." Connor nodded gently. "But listen - if you do need help, come to the Singing Horse - it's a nightclub in Redbridge. Ask for me - the owner knows me."
			"Why are you doing this?" she asked, her brow furrowing.
			"Doing what? Being kind?"
			"Yes! Why would you do that?!" she hissed.
			"Because... I know what it's like to be tortured." he shrugged. "And to be hunted. And it's my fault you're in this situation. And... well, I'm something of a superhero. It's my *job* to be kind. Besides, it sounds like we're both in the business of killing Super-Agents."
			She paused, looking at him up and down. The monster in the kevlar suit - her target, her prey... it didn't make sense.
			She hesitantly reached out her hand. He paused, but took it, and their consciousnesses shot against each other.
			She saw the Commandant's torment of him. His body twisting and reshaping against his will. He saw... nothing. The horror of nothingness. The pod.
			It was too much. They pulled away, and rubbed their temples in unison.
			She turned away, then turned her head back. She pulled off her domino mask, and gulped.
			"Before they took me..." she began, choking on her words. "My name was Gwen. Gwen Blake."
			Connor hesitated, but his mask rippled and melted away.
			"I'm Connor. Connor Barrett."
			Whiplash - Gwen - bowed her head, and walked away into the night.
			Connor stood there, as she faded into the fog. The kevlar melted back down into his soft red hoodie, and he pulled the cloth closer for warmth. He took a deep breath, and smiled sadly.

			Ivan watched through his scope, his black-veined eyes tensing. He took a deep breath, and pulled Isabella's trigger.
			Many people have claimed to be the best shot in the world. Few could make a claim like Ivan.
			The bullet sailed from his makeshift nest atop Rydon Tower. It ripped through the air, smashing through an office window, and then another on the other side. It burned a hole into a balcony cover, and passed through the gaps on a metal ladder. It whizzed past Naismith's ear, lightly grazed Connor's neck, and finally slammed into the pistol's barrel.
			He gasped in pain, looking down at the gun as it backfired in his hand. Amy's ear rang from the blast, but she knew exactly what to do. She leaned her head forward, and slammed it backwards, smearing his nose across his face.
			Connor pounced forward, as she broke free from his grip. He wrapped his hands around the neck, and squeezed.

			He raised him up in the air. Chapman frantically kicked, to no avail.
			"Do you? *Do you?*" Connor repeated, his grip tightening.
			Naismith walked over.
			"Let him down." he said gently.
			"Good one."
			"I'm serious. Let him down." Naismith repeated.
			"I am too." Connor snarled, his eyes a blazing scarlet.
			"You think he doesn't want you to kill him?" Naismith began. "You think cowards like this would rather face trial? No. Don't you dare take the chance to look him in the eye from the people whose loved ones he's stolen. Don't. You. Dare."
			Connor growled like a rabid dog. But then, Amy gently put her hand on his shoulder.
			"He's right. Let him down." she whispered. "I'm okay. I'm not hurt."
			Connor's eyes slowly dimmed, still blazing. He finally released his grip.
			"Gah..." Chapman sputtered. "Coward... you think you're one of them? Admit it... you're more like me. You *enjoy* it."
			"Shut the fuck up." Naismith barked, pistol-whipping him. He slammed him against the wall, and cuffed him.
			"It's alright... he'll face justice for this." Amy said softly.
			Connor hesitated, his eyes dancing over Naismith's gun.
			The image flooded his mind - grabbing it and shooting this bastard.
			No. No more guns. He didn't have many rules left, but he had to stick to the ones that remained.
			Then, a wicked grin cracked under his mask. He turned, and gripped Chapman's crossed palms, before crushing them.
			His screams filled the air, before a claw-blade skewered through the palms. Connor twisted the blade, severing muscle and splintering broken bone. Another slice, and fingertips fell down - the same ones he'd stolen from Lydia.
			Chapman cried even more. Then, he went silent as Connor closed his mouth forcefully.
			"You took with these hands, and I take them in turn." Connor snarled viciously. "You'll never, ever take a life with these again. They'll never heal. Not right, at least. Every time you try to grip, you'll feel a shooting pain, and you'll remember *ME.* You're right about one thing - I do enjoy it. I enjoy cleaning up *filth* like you."
			"Alright, enough." Naismith said half-heartedly, dragging the sobbing monster away.

			Connor looked back at the people in the shadows, his eyes cutting through the dark. The humans struggled to find their bearings.
			Before he could move, Kat stepped forward. She was holding her jaw, but her eyes were steady.
			"Thank you." she said quietly. "For stopping him."
			Lexi nodded beside her, Sage still clinging to her arm.
			"You saved us again." Lexi added. "First the fire, now this. I don't know who you are under that mask, but... thank you."
			Connor didn't say anything. He just nodded, once.
			Then he sighed, and melded into the darkness. He morphed back into clothes, and crept over with catlike tread, just as Sparky set the lights back on.
			"Oh, thank god... it's over." Bea sighed, starting a group hug.
			Connor hesitated, but joined in. When it broke, he embraced his sister. She returned it.
			"I'm sorry..." he said, tearing up.
			"It's okay... it's not like I wanted you to get shot." she chuckled, giving him a knowing nod.
			"Still..." he sighed. "I'm your big brother, it's my job to protect you."
			"You're 6 months older." she grinned.
			"Still counts."
			Across the room, Kat was helping Lexi to her feet. Her lip was split, and her hands were shaking, but she was standing. Sage had made her way over, and was hugging them both.
			"Everyone okay?" Tommy called out, moving through the crowd.
			"I think so." Kat nodded, wincing as she touched her jaw. "Just bruises."
			"Speak for yourself." Lexi muttered, rubbing her scalp. "That bastard..."

			"It's over." Tommy nodded. "You're safe."

			"I'll leave you to it, tovarishch." Ivan grinned.

			"Don't cry, Verdict. You're still my favourite sniper." Connor snarked.
			"Fucking better be, tovarishch." Ivan quipped. "Spokoynoy nochi."
			Connor nodded, shut the door, and walked over to his sister. He gently stroked her hair, and sat down.
			Then, he listened to her heartbeat. Just listened to it. Savoured it. Appreciated it.
			Loved it.

Behold, the hire of the labourers who have reaped your fields, which you kept back by fraud, crieth; and the cries of those who have reaped have entered into the ears of the Lord of Sabaoth. 			Geraldine looked on, and smiled proudly.

Their motions resembled a pulley system as much as they did monstrous heroes.

			Sparky tilted his head. "Can you understand me?" he asked, longingly.
			"Hah... I wish I could speak dog." she chuckled. "I don't know what that was, but it sounded like a question."
			He sighed, and whined slightly. "It's okay. I don't need you to understand me to have a good time with you. I get to be a person with Connor - maybe I can just be a dog with you."
			Chloe smiled warmly. "Clever boy. Chatty boy!" she grinned, giving him a treat. He greedily ate it - a bacon-flavoured cheese twist - his favourite.
			"Don't tell your dad." she smirked.
			"Oh, I've told him." Sparky replied cheekily. "He thinks it's really sweet."
			She pulled out her bag, and checked her blood sugar. 3.8. She sipped a sugary drink, zipped up her jacket, and stood.

			Over in Redbridge, Connor effortlessly carried a stack of crates into the garage, while Amy struggled to bring in two.
			"Fuh... fuck..." she panted. "Wish I had super-strength."
			"You're doing fine." he said softly. "I appreciate it."
			"I'd be doing better if I still had the super-suit..." she teased.
			"Very funny."
			Amy chuckled, and opened up a crate. She pulled out a photograph of a blonde woman, smiling on a park bench. Next to her was Vince - younger, and grinning giddily.
			"Aw..." she nodded. "Thank fuck that didn't get damaged."
			"Hey, mum." Connor smiled softly.
			Amy gently brushed his shoulder. "She'd be proud."
			"Yours would be, too." Connor nodded.
			She shrugged. "I kinda wish I knew more about her. I mean... I wish I had an uncle like Vince who could tell me all about her."
			Connor hesitated. "You know... I can look into it, if you like?"
			Amy paused, then smiled. "That... that'd be really nice, actually."
			Connor nodded. "Now come on." he grinned. "Let's get a few more in before your shift starts."

			Chloe finally came to a stop at the Danwich train station. She sat down on the bench, and breathed out. Sparky curled up in the seat next to her, and rested his head on her lap, looking up at her.
			"Hey, buddy..." Chloe smiled, stroking his head. "You're a good boy, aren't you?"
			"I'm told I'm the best." he grinned.
			Chloe chuckled. "Yeah, you know you're a good boy, don't you? Your dad's a lucky man, huh? Getting to do walks like this with you every day. I should look after you more often!"
			"You know..." she began. "I think I'm really starting to like him."
			She looked down at Sparky, who was listening intently. "Since the day we met, I've always thought he was sweet... but, it wasn't until recently that I started to realise just how much I like him."
			She stared off into the distance. "He's always been so good to me. I should just talk to him about it, shouldn't I?"
			"Yes! Yes, tell him! Or I will!" Sparky barked excitedly.
			"Haha, you think I should, huh?" she smirked. "Maybe I will."

			At that, Sparky raised a paw, and pushed it into Chloe's chest.
			"Oh, look at me... I'm trauma-dumping to a dog." she chuckled, taking his paw. "Thank God the platform's empty, or I'd get a lot of funny looks, eh?"

			"What's up? Do you want something?" she asked - somehow sensing his expression of desire.
			"Oh, the mind-merge!" he gasped. "Can you hear me?!"
			She tilted her head, and stroked his mane.
			Part of her - a tiny part - got a hint of what he said. That part was quickly ordered to banish the thought.
			After all, dogs can't talk. They can't. Right?
			He sighed. "Of course... the link has to be two-way, and I can't ask you to let me in."
			"Hey..." she cooed, scratching behind his ears. "You're a good boy."
			He pressed his head into her hands, and closed his eyes.
			Eh. Being a dog wasn't so bad, actually.
			She leant back. After a short while, she got a buzz on her phone - Bea was calling her.
			"Hey, beauts!"
			"Hey hey!" Chloe answered, smiling. "You okay?"

			At the mention of his name, Chloe cringed slightly.
			"Yeah, sounds good. How is he with dogs?"
			"I'm not sure - but I'm sure he'll love Sparky!"
			With that, a train crept over the horizon.
			"Cool! I'll see you in a bit."
			Part of her was simply excited to hang out with Bea.
			A bigger part was ready to learn more about Charlie.

Do not - Bea, I repeat - do NOT trust him."

In fact, the Bockas used to have a contract with the mortal villagers; the humans would give them offerings, and they would protect them from disease. The Bocka Dhu, however, just took what they wanted with nothing in return. But one day, their king got too greedy, and robbed a Dragon's nest - Dragons were like Gods to the Fae. The Dragon was displeased with this insult, and so he said to the Bocka King;

			"Thou hast taken what was mine,
			Wretched Bocka with fire-eyes,
			Midnight shall mark thy doom.
			Stand before me, or,
			Let thy clan be swept away,
			Like leaves in the wyrd-wind."

			The Bocka King was disturbed by this proclamation. He loved his clan, but knew he would die should he face the Dragon. So, he devised a cunning scheme...
			The King approached the chief of the human villagers, and gave them an offer - all the gold and silver in the mountain, and in exchange, the humans would slay the dragon.
			No human was brave enough to accept the offer. Until finally, a young man stood, and agreed.
			That night, the Dragon descended upon the peak of the mountain. The young man stood defiantly. The Dragon was not amused.

			"Thing of flesh, I know thee not.
			My quarrel is not thine.
			Leave these lands,
			Or feel fire's bite.
			Thy fate is nought to me,
			Scurrow back to thy folk!"

			The man stood firm, and drew his blade. The Dragon could not help but be impressed. The two fought, and the Dragon took to the sky, holding the young man in his hand.
			The young man was brave. He took his blade, and plunged it into the Dragon's throat. A mighty roar shook the foundations of the land.
			Seeing this, the Bocka King rejoiced.

			"Look, my people, and see man's folly!
			Tricked by promises of wealth and fame.
			Such simple fools, who bask in the light!
			Thralls to the Earthborne, as is proper.
			His death brings riches beyond measure.
			Let our cry ring out - Long Live the Bockas!"

			Hearing this, the man was enraged at the Bockas' deception. As the Dragon fell to the ground, he turned his blade, steering the Dragon towards the mountain.
			It hit the peak, landing right on the Bocka King. The mountain was shattered, leaving the valley underneath to run into the sea. The old mountain was named the Wyrm's Rock, and the new valley was called the Draca Hills.

			The hero's body had been torn down to specks by the explosion. But seeped in magma and dragon blood, and the screaming souls of a thousand Bocka Dhu, he rose again. He pulled his blade from the peak, like Arthur did with Excalibur. It, like its master, had been reforged; now glowing with magical energy and coated in obsidian. The tribes united under his shadow, and as draconic wings unfurled from his back, he soared upwards, blocking out the moon."

			Finishing the tale, Connor looked up at his friends. Chloe was looking at him, almost dreamily.
			"Or at least, that's the legend, anyway." he cleared his throat.
			"You missed your calling as a storyteller." she grinned. He chuckled.
			"I love that story, man. Except, I can never remember the hero's name." Trey stroked his chin.
			"Traditionally, you call him Pendrinn. When the Saxons came over, they changed it to Wulfric Wyrmsbane." Connor explained. "Most tellings of the story have him become a guardian spirit of the valley. Supposedly, it rains when he flaps his wings."
			"Well, the bastard needs to stop flapping his wings. It's been pissing it down lately." Trey grinned.
			"I love old folklore like that." Chloe smiled. "You have to wonder, who comes up with that?"
			"Well, it's not so far fetched." Trey began. "This valley has an unusually high amount of silver and gold ore."
			"And fossils." Connor added. "In the Wyrmrock caves, they've found loads of weird fossils. Mostly, they look like animals - but some also look like people. Except... weird. And also, the fossils were found in the same parts - meaning they're the same age."
			Chloe leant back, surprised. "That's insane. How is that not bigger news?"
			"Well, I saw a documentary on that." Trey replied. "They reckon there was some disease that caused these deformities in the valley."
			"I heard about that. Didn't that same doc also prove that Wyrmrock *was* just a foothill to a much bigger mountain here that blew up?" Connor asked.
			"It's a weird one. They proved that there was something similar to an asteroid impact 50,000 years ago that created the valley - but, the valley doesn't look the way it should do from something like that. They're not sure if it was a really weirdly shaped asteroid, or if the mountain's structure caused the unusual valley.. One of life's great mysteries." Trey grinned.
			"The age of the story is also weird." Connor added. "Like, the fact that it references an ancient mountain being destroyed by an aerial impact, *and* we're pretty sure it predates Celtic settlement in the region - so it's possible that the story started out from the oral traditions of a tribe who actually witnessed the impact. Then the Celts come over and add Bockas to the mix, and then the Saxons come over and change up the names... it's pretty cool, when you think about it. There's even a theory that Pendrinn coming back from the dead to watch over us was a product of Christianisation. And, to boot, House Calder claimed lineage from him - though that's obviously dubious."
			"House Calder?" Chloe tilted her head. "You've mentioned them before, right?"
			"Former Lords of the valley." Trey explained. "Descendants of the Caledwyri tribe - Pendrinn's people. The locals largely assimilated after the Saxon conquest, while their ruling clan was exiled to Brittany - they became a merchant family who bribed Church officials to legitimise them as House Calder, a minor noble house. When William the Conqueror came up, they helped finance the war and provided their House Guard as mercenaries - in exchange, they were reinstated as rulers of the valley - the Counts of Drackhill."
			"That is, until Lord Calder XIII went mad." Connor chuckled. "But that's a story for another day."
			"I've got time." Chloe grinned.

			"House Calder ruled us from 1066 to 1309. Lord Calder was the most corrupt of them all - and he was untouchable. He'd fabricated dirt on any rival in the valley - which meant his family controlled all the banks, the guilds, the markets, the land, and most importantly - the church. He had his second son installed as Grandmaster of the Order of Lazarus - a borderline-heretical holy order - in direct defiance of the Concordat of London. The conflict between secular lords and religious leaders was heating up in this era; but Calder was so powerful, he could appoint and dismiss abbots and bishops as he pleased. He paid lip service to his status as a vassal of Edward Longshanks and, later, Edward II - but in truth, he was an absolute monarch. Arguably, the first - predating Louis XIV by over 300 years. According to the story, he believed that something priceless was buried beneath the city. Ironically, the excavations he funded benefitted the working classes, since it gave them plenty of work; and the valley's high quantity of precious metals made the Guilds rich - but the taxes he levied against the other nobles to fund this endeavour angered them. They cooked up some accusations of witchcraft and even cannibalism, but the Order protected him from the worst of it. Until, that is - they found it."
			He paused for effect, and Trey grinned as Chloe waited politely. Finally, her curiosity got the better of her etiquette.
			"Found what?"
			"Deep in the newborn Underhill, beneath all the earlier tunnels, they found what Lord Calder believed was the Dragon's heart. He had a dungeon built there - one so big, it was basically an underground castle. House Calder moved down there almost in its entirety - the Lord kept secluding himself in its chambers, which were so extensive, the Order would send messengers down for him, and they'd die of starvation on the way down. That's why the Mayor is the chief executive of the entire valley - back then, the Mayor of Drackhill City had to become the de facto Earl in order to keep the valley running. Worse, the workers in the Underhill began reporting screams coming from the Lord's chambers, loud enough to be heard from the sewer drains on the surface; and people started going missing. Rumours of arcane experiments and alchemical augmentation grew - there were whispers that Lord Calder had ensorcelled the long-dead Bocka Dhu, and sold his soul to the Devil."
			Trey leaned forwards, as if he were a wrestler tagging in. "They started to believe those accusations of witchcraft and cannibalism were true. When Longshanks died, the nobility petitioned Edward II to restrain Lord Calder's powers. But the new king had troubles of his own - the war in Scotland was going badly, his barons were growing restless, and nobody at court was eager to start shit with the most powerful lord in the country. So, the nobles struck out on their own, riled up a mob, and stormed the Undercastle - and the House Guard, each one towering over the peasant levies, hacked them to pieces."
			"Damn. I mean, that's pretty standard when you send torches and pitchforks against armed knights." she shrugged.

			"Lord Calder was experimenting on people and creating half-demon super-knights, but the dog bit is where you get squeamish?"

			"Oh, so do I. I just think the rest is grim, too." Trey snarked.

"Calder's abuse of power, combined with Edward II's own autocratic tendencies, led to the Ordinances of 1311 that restricted the king's power to unilaterally appoint whoever to whatever. Calder became an abject example of how badly that can go. At the same time, they modelled Drackhill's new system on the Holy Roman Empire's Free Cities, becoming an autonomous government within England. Even after the Ordinances were repealed in 1322, the new semi-republican system remained. During the Civil War, the valley supported Parliament, and so maintained its autonomy even after Feudalism started its slow death. It wasn't until the Victorian era that the system was replaced, but even then, the valley kept its distance from Westminster. Come 1974, we got put in this awkward halfway between a normal county and a devolved government."

That means, even if I only have 1 chromosome, I can compare it and tell what species it came from. But the Werewolf's chromosomes - most of them have completely separate markers. As though they evolved completely independent of each other - and of any life on Earth."

			"I... I can't rule it out." Chloe admitted. "But he's not human, that's for sure."

			Connor nodded softly, and gently brushed her hand. She blushed.
			"I'm sorry about earlier... I just, I'm fed up with her. She acts like she's the mother from heaven and I'm the daughter from hell."
			"It's okay. Really, it is. Besides, like I said, my uncle's in prison. It's not like I can sit in judgement on other people's family dynamics."
			Chloe chuckled. "Well, at least your uncle sounds alright. Hey, speaking of... last night, you said there's the law, and then there's right and wrong. I... I didn't mean to imply that I was judging you and your uncle." she said, looking down shyly.
			"Oh? I didn't even think of that - it's okay." Connor smiled. Chloe looked relieved.
			"That's good." she smiled. "I was worried that it might come off as some... I don't know, like I was trying to insult you in the subtext? Which I wasn't, to be clear." she stammered.
			"Oh, god, don't do that - you wanna insult me, your best bet is just saying it openly. You know me and subtext." Connor chuckled. Chloe smirked.
			"Hah, forgot about that. I'll bear that in mind." she said. "To be honest, it's refreshing."
			"Oh?"
			"Well... I don't have to worry about subtext with you. I know that when you say something, there's no hidden meaning. And I don't have to worry about how you'll take something I say, either." she explained.
			"I guess being autistic as all hell has some advantages." Connor grinned.
			Both laughed, enjoying the moment.
			"Do I need to call your grandad 'my Lord,' or something?"
			She chuckled. "No. I mean, he *is* a Lord, but he never cared for it. He's on medical leave from Parliament, at the moment. When he... when the time comes, it'll pass down to my dad, and then one day, me. The Barony of Derrington is absolute primogeniture instead of male-preference, meaning I'm the expected heir."
			"Damn." Connor raised his eyebrows. "You gonna take it?"
			"I... I don't know how much of a say I get." she admitted. "But, if I get the choice, I'll pass. There are quite a few paths I'd be happy to see my life go down, but being even more enmeshed in the aristocracy is definitely not one of them."
			"Hey, I'll take it. Except, Baron Barrett sounds silly." he quipped.
			She giggled, and leaned back - relaxed, a little.
			"Hey, before you head off - there's something I wanna show you." she said. "It's a short walk away - I don't suppose you have any boots?"
			"Yeah, in the car." he nodded. "I'll grab Sparky, and meet you outside?"
			She smiled, and he headed into the garden. There, Sparky was basking in the cold sunlight.
			"Morning, buddy." he smiled.
			"Morning!" Sparky yapped. "Are we heading home, now?"
			"Yeah, in a minute." Connor nodded. "Chloe's gonna show us something, though."
			"Oh, okay." Sparky yawned, rising. Connor morphed on a pair of boots, and they headed into the driveway.

			The walk was fairly uneventful - the three were still tired, and enjoyed the cold air waking them. Chloe held Molly on a leash, while Sparky trotted to their heels.
			"Hah..." she chuckled. "Funny how the wolfdog is more well-behaved. If she was off lead right now, she'd be spending the next three hours stuck in a rabbit hole."
			"Ah, it's a size thing. Rabbits aren't nutritious enough for Sparky." Connor grinned. "If there was a horse here, then maybe."
			"What's a 'horse?'" Sparky tilted his head.
			"He doesn't chase horses, does he?" she turned quickly.
			"Hm? Oh, no - I was taking the piss." Connor shrugged.
			Chloe laughed, and they kept walking.
			It didn't take too long before they arrived at the pasture. She knelt down, and unleashed Molly, who was wagging her tail in anticipation.
			"Bucephalus!" she called out.
			Connor cocked an eyebrow, before a bellowing neigh cried out, and the thundering of hooves filled the air. A small shelter in the corner of the pasture shook with movement, and a massive black stallion charged out.
			"Oh." Sparky tilted his head. "That's a big deer."
			Connor stifled a chuckle, and bowed his head. Bucephalus raced over to Chloe, and pushed his head into her chest. She planted her boots in the mud as he pushed her backwards, before nuzzling.
			"Hey, Bucey!" she cooed. "How have you been, baby boy?"
			He nickered as he rubbed against her, and then took a look at Connor.
			"Hey, buddy." he smiled, approaching towards an angle. Bucephalus tilted his head to the side, keeping his eye on Connor. Connor averted his gaze, and raised his hand up softly, towards the horse's mouth.
			"This is Connor." Chloe said softly. "Say hi!"
			Bucephalus moved forward slightly, and nickered again as he sniffed Connor's hand.
			"Good boy." Connor whispered, gently rubbing the withers. Molly yipped at his heels, and then started sniffing Bucephalus's rear. Connor went to grab her, but relaxed as the horse seemed unbothered by the fuss - he wasn't much of a kicker, it seemed.
			"You're good with him." Chloe noted, beaming.
			"My cousin Mickey knew a fella with a very similar horse." Connor explained. "He's not a pure Shire, is he?"
			"Oh of course, I remember you mentioned spending time with horses as a kid." she smiled. "And yeah, well spotted. He's half Shire, half Arabian."
			"...either something terrible happened, or the bravest Arabian of all time managed to get his hooves on a stepladder." Connor grinned.
			Chloe burst into laughter, and Bucephalus whinnied too, almost mimicking.
			"He's a good mix." Connor cleared his throat. "He's got a Shire's build and temperament, but his facial expressions look more Arabian to me. I'm guessing he's a smart lad?"
			"Oh yeah, he's clever." she beamed. "He's a really good listener."
			"Do you ride him often?"
			"No, he's Victor's." she shrugged. "But he prefers me."
			Bucephalus neighed, as if in agreement. Connor chuckled, and scratched him gently by the nape of his neck.
			"I like the name." Connor smiled. "I'm sure good old Alexander would think he's a worthy bearer of the title."
			"Ugh, that might be the one thing you and Victor have in common - you both know who the original Bucephalus was." she grinned.
			"Hey, my dog's name is Spartacus, so I can't judge." he smirked back. "Does Victor know it means 'Ox-headed?'"
			She laughed. "You know, the name might be more fitting now. I've never met an animal as stubborn as ol' Bucey."
			The horse grunted in protest, and pushed his head back into her.
			"Hey! You know it's true!" she chuckled, pushing back against him. True to his name, he didn't budge.
			Sparky gently approached, and raised his snout upwards. The two animals sniffed each other, and Bucephalus moved his head away.
			"I think he likes us." Sparky shrugged.
			Chloe chuckled. "Anyway, there you have it. You've met the Derringtons, now."
			Connor smiled warmly. "It's been really nice. Hey... don't feel like you have to hide your family from me, or any of us, okay? None of us would've judged you over it."
			"I know." she nodded, hesitating. "I... judge *myself* over it. I hate the whole thing. The whole stupid system, the attitude, the ideology..."
			Connor reached his hand over Bucephalus's back, and placed it on hers. She blushed, and looked down.
			"None of that is *you,* okay?" he said quietly. "Yes, us down in Drackhill are more... well, we're not exactly huge lovers of the class system, or the aristocracy. But *you* are not part of that. As far as any of us care, you're Chloe - our mate, who shows up when we need her; who has a couple of vodkas and can start out-infodumping me; who's always looking out for all of us. *That's* the Chloe we know - and nothing I've learned in the last 24 hours changes that."
			Her eyes fluttered, and she looked into his eyes. She squeezed his hand, before grimacing.
			"Ew! Bucey! Way to ruin the moment!" she laughed, as a dollop of manure plopped onto the grass.
			They both burst into laughter, as Bucephalus trotted away. Then, they embraced.
			"I'll see you after New Year's, yeah?" she smiled.
			"Yeah. I'll see you then." he beamed. With that, they parted.
